The validation results based on C-band Sentinel-1 data and in situ measurements demonstrate that the proposed NCD method achieves retrieval performance comparable to the traditional STCD approach, despite the limited information provided by a single-temporal acquisition. The retrieval results yield root mean square errors of 0.068 m3/m3 and 0.072 m3/m3 for the two soil moisture monitoring networks, with correlation coefficients of 0.74 and 0.58, respectively. Moreover, the NCD method exhibits particularly strong robustness under conditions of relatively low soil moisture and limited variability in its temporal dynamics. The proposed NCD algorithm further reduces the complexity of data acquisition and processing, offering a complementary alternative for near real-time soil moisture mapping in support of emergency applications.

title: Hydrological drivers of silicate weathering in snow-dominated alpine headwater catchments with variable forest cover (Tatra Mountains, Western Carpathians)
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Agnieszka Rajwa-Kuligiewicz, Artur Kuligiewicz, Marek Duliński, Kazimierz Różański
abstract: This study quantifies silicate weathering rates (SWR) and carbon dioxide capture rates (CCR) in mid-latitude mountains with seasonal snow cover, with particular focus on snowmelt-driven weathering and vegetation effects. The study was conducted in headwater catchments within the crystalline core of the Tatra Mountains (Carpathians), which share similar lithology but differ in forest cover and disturbance history. The study combined geochemical modeling with isotope-based analyses, including mean transit time (MTT) estimation using stable water isotopes and tritium, together with mixing–splitting analysis. The tritium-derived MTT was ∼3.7 years, reflecting dominant winter baseflow conditions, whereas MTT estimated from the sine-wave method yielded much shorter times (0.4–2.4 years), likely due to stronger relative contribution of shorter flow paths. Mean SWR ranged from 5.19 ± 0.14 t/km2/yr to 7.60 ± 0.29 t/km2/yr, while CCR ranged from 2.58 ± 0.23 × 104 to 3.76 ± 0.33 × 104 mol/km2/yr. The results indicate a kinetically limited weathering regime in which reaction kinetics and MTT exert stronger controls on weathering fluxes than discharge or catchment area. SWR and dissolution rates varied among catchments, with the forested catchment exhibiting higher weathering rates, longer MTT, lower young water fractions, and greater contribution of winter precipitation to summer discharge. Mean annual evapotranspiration (ET) ranged from ∼42% in the mature forest to ∼60% in the regenerating stand. Because summer precipitation with a relatively high 18O/16O ratio was preferentially lost to ET, the isotopic composition of water contributing to weathering was biased towards winter precipitation with a relatively low 18O/16O ratio.

title: Depth-dependent thermal management of a medium-deep coaxial borehole heat exchanger using segmented inner-pipe insulation and enhanced grout conductivity
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Jianjun Sun, Yiming Li, Guiqiu Song
abstract: Medium-deep coaxial borehole heat exchangers are limited by internal thermal short-circuiting, especially in shallow sections where the upward return flow loses heat to the colder descending flow. This study develops a depth-dependent wellbore thermal management strategy that combines segmented inner-pipe insulation, enhanced grout thermal conductivity, and flow-rate optimization for a 2500 m coaxial geothermal well in Shenyang, China. A semi-analytical heat-transfer model was established and validated against field tests at flow rates of 15.5, 20.5, and 26.0 m³/h, which measured heat extraction rates of 242.2, 309.7, and 353.2 kW, respectively. Baseline diagnosis shows that the shallow section contributes little useful heat gain while intensifying return-flow heat loss. A three-zone inner-pipe configuration, with insulation in the upper 750 m, increases heat extraction to approximately 385 kW and maintains a performance evaluation coefficient above 1.0. Increasing grout conductivity from 2.70 to 4.0 W/(m·K) further improves heat output, and combining it with segmented insulation yields a positive non-additive gain. A recommended flow-rate range of 24–27 m³/h is identified by balancing heat extraction and pumping power. Thermal recovery analysis indicates that the formation recovers to 32–33°C after 6–7 days of rest, with a projected annual recovery ratio above 76% over 20 years. These results show that depth-dependent coordination of pipe insulation, grout conductivity, and circulation flow can improve the performance and sustainability of medium-deep coaxial geothermal heating systems.

title: Experimental study of anisotropic behavior of biotite-ordered granite under thermally-coupled true triaxial compression conditions in deep geothermal boreholes
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Yongping Li, Houyu Wang, Hongyuan Zhou, Ming Wu, Zaobao Liu
abstract: The anisotropic mechanical behavior of granite under thermal-mechanical coupling remains poorly understood for the design of deep wellbores in high-temperature geothermal reservoirs, such as those in the Tibetan Plateau. This study experimentally investigates the biotite-induced anisotropy in strength, deformation, and failure modes of granite subjected to true triaxial compression under coupled thermal–mechanical conditions. Experiments were conducted at temperatures of 20, 100, 150, and 190 °C, with minor principal stresses ranging from 10 to 40 MPa, reflecting typical in-situ reservoir conditions. Two loading configurations were designed to examine the effect of the orientation between the intermediate principal stress and the biotite foliation. The results reveal that the orientation of the intermediate principal stress significantly governs the anisotropic behavior. As the minimum principal stress increased, the strength anisotropy coefficient decreased from 0.29 to 0.07. Increasing temperature from 20 °C to 190 °C reduced the strength by approximately 42%, while the strength anisotropy coefficient decreased from 0.18 to 0.02, suggesting a progressive weakening of the controlling effect of the dominant biotite foliation under thermo-mechanical conditions. These findings improve the understanding of the thermo-mechanical anisotropic behavior of biotite-ordered granite and provide useful insights for the design and stability evaluation of deep geothermal wellbores.

title: Damage evolution of thermal shock in granite for enhanced geothermal systems
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Liuke Huang, Guolin Rong, Xingchuan Liao, Nailing Xiu, Haifeng Fu, Dingwei Weng, Ling Yu
abstract: Cold-fluid injection in enhanced geothermal systems (EGS) can induce transient thermal shock in hot dry rock, thereby altering the mechanical behavior of the reservoir. However, the coupled influence of thermal shock and confining pressure on granite, as well as the associated microstructural damage mechanisms, remains insufficiently understood. In this study, outcrop granite from the Sichuan Basin was subjected to multi-level high-temperature treatment followed by transient thermal shock tests with different temperature differences. A combination of macroscopic mechanical testing and microstructural characterization using scanning electron microscopy was used to investigate thermal damage evolution from the grain scale to the sample scale. The results show that thermal shock significantly reduces granite strength. After heating to 200 °C and subsequent cooling to 25 °C, the uniaxial compressive strength drops by approximately 38.4%, a reduction far exceeding that caused by heating alone. This weakening effect was markedly suppressed by confining pressure. At 20 MPa confining pressure, the specimen shocked from 400°C to 25°C retained a compressive strength of 395.2 MPa, comparable to that of the room-temperature specimen, 392.4 MPa. Microstructural observations indicate that thermal damage evolves through four stages, from initial crack closure and grain-boundary adjustment to crack propagation and thermally induced degradation. These findings contribute to a better understanding of the thermo-mechanical damage mechanisms in granite and provide a reference dataset for similar parametric studies and numerical model calibration.

title: Machine learning-driven optimization of production-injection scheme: A case study of geothermal doublet system in Yangling, Guanzhong Basin
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Jia Liu, Sen Li, Yi Xue, Chenyang Duan, Shi-Tong Li, Yin Wang, Zhen-Kun Liu
abstract: As a sustainable clean energy source, geothermal energy is widely distributed with large reserves, which can be used in diverse applications. The optimization of the well production-injection scheme is crucial for the efficient production of this type of energy. This case study focuses on a geothermal development project in the Yangling District, Guanzhong Basin. Geological exploration and well data collection are first conducted to understand the occurrence characteristics and geological structure background of the geothermal resource in the district. Using the 1D line element theory for the analysis of 3D wellbore structure, a coupled thermo-hydro-mechanical (THM) model is established in the finite element software, COMSOL. The numerical model can accurately simulate the production-injection process of the geothermal doublet system. Subsequently, a surrogate model is developed to relate production-injection parameters to reservoir responses. Trained through the deep neural network (DNN) of machine learning, the surrogate model’s validity and accuracy are demonstrated by comparing its predicted values with 500 numerically obtained (“true”) values, where larger data sets result in better predictive performance. Further, combining machine learning with 4 optimization algorithms, the production-injection scheme is optimized based on production-injection parameters and objective functions. The revenues (final objective function) obtained by these optimization algorithms are nearly identical, outperforming 95% of true value samples, which shows the reliability and efficiency of the proposed method in determining the optimal production-injection scheme. The study insightfully promotes the intelligent transformation of geothermal energy development.

title: Experimental investigation on energy mechanical evolution and damage model of red limestone subjected to high-temperature water cooling cycling
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Haopeng Jiang, Hui Wang, Fengrui Zhang, Wei Yin
abstract: In geothermal development and high-temperature rock engineering, sedimentary geothermal surrounding rocks are prone to mechanical deterioration and damage accumulation under long-term high temperature effects, cold water recharge, and thermal-water circulation disturbances. In this study, red limestone collected from Ya’an, Sichuan Province, was investigated through a series of triaxial compression tests after exposure to different temperatures (200 °C, 400 °C, 600 °C, and 800 °C) and varying numbers of water-quenching cycles (0, 5, and 10). The degradation of the physical and mechanical properties of the limestone was systematically evaluated, and its energy evolution characteristics, including energy input, storage, dissipation, and release, were analyzed within the framework of energy dissipation theory. The results show that both the peak strength and elastic modulus of the red limestone decrease noticeably with increasing temperature and quenching cycles. The repeated action of thermal stress and rapid cooling promotes crack initiation and propagation between mineral grains, increases porosity, and leads to pronounced deterioration of the internal microstructure. In terms of energy behavior, the progressive accumulation of damage weakens the rock energy storage capacity and significantly raises the proportion of dissipated energy. Based on the experimental results, a statistical damage constitutive model incorporating a modified energy dissipation function was established. The validation results indicate that the proposed model can effectively characterize the nonlinear deformation behavior and strength response of red limestone after high-temperature water-cooling treatment. These findings provide an important theoretical basis for the efficient development of geothermal resources and the stability evaluation of high-temperature rock engineering.

title: Quantifying geothermal heat loss at the Dayoukeng crater using UAV thermal imaging and comparison with Landsat-derived estimates
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Hai-Po Chan, Yu-Chang Chan, Cheng-Wei Sun
abstract: This study quantifies geothermal radiative heat flux (RHF) and geothermal radiative heat loss (RHL) at the Dayoukeng (DYK) crater of Tatun Volcanic Group (TVG) in Taiwanusing both UAV thermal imaging and Landsat thermal infrared data. A dawn UAV survey minimized solar effects, acquiring 782 thermal images at 13 cm resolution. Land surface temperatures from both datasets were used to estimate RHF accounting for surface emissivity, atmospheric transmittance, and ambient temperature. Both datasets consistently delineate geothermal anomalies, while UAV imagery uniquely resolves fine-scale thermal heterogeneity. Maximum temperatures reach 84.4 °C in UAV data and 44.4 °C in Landsat, corresponding to peak RHF values of 214 and 62.6 Wm⁻², respectively. Despite differences in spatial resolution and peak values, geothermal heat loss estimates are comparable, with RHL of 210 MW derived from UAV data and 217 MW from Landsat observations, and are of similar order of magnitude to previous geochemical estimates based on the volumetric method. These results demonstrate that satellite thermal imagery provides an efficient tool for regional geothermal heat loss assessment, whereas UAV thermal imaging offers substantially enhanced detail on localized heat flux variability. This study presents the first UAV-based geothermal heat loss assessment at DYK within the Tatun Volcanic Group, northern Taiwan, and highlights the complementary strengths of UAV and satellite thermal observations for geothermal exploration and volcanic monitoring.

title: Limited heat connectivity across the Northeastern Segment of the Tanlu Fault, China: Implications for low–temperature geothermal systems
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Jingyu Lin, Xuelian Huang, Shuai Wang, Shihua Qi, Xu Wang
abstract: The northeastern segment of the Tanlu Fault (NTLF) hosts predominantly low–temperature geothermal systems, contrasting with the high–temperature resources in the central and southern segments. To elucidate the factors controlling the low–temperature characteristics in the NTLF, we combined geochemical and isotopic analyses of geothermal and cold groundwater with numerical simulations. The results indicate that the geothermal waters are primarily recharged through meteoric water infiltration, with reservoir temperatures ranging from 60 °C to 110 °C and circulation depths extending from 1539 to 2972 m. Hydrogeochemical and isotopic evidence suggests prolonged water–rock interaction, relatively slow groundwater renewal, and limited contribution from high–temperature magmatic or deep hydrothermal fluids. Numerical simulations show that, under limited effective fault permeability, upward heat transfer from deeper thermal domains to shallow and intermediate reservoirs remains weak, and the temperature field is mainly controlled by conductive heat transfer. Sensitivity analyses further support that fault permeability strongly influences the efficiency of upward heat transfer. This study highlights that the geothermal significance of major fault zones depends not only on their structural scale, but also on effective fault connectivity that enables upward heat transfer.

title: Distribution characteristics and controlling factors of the thermal field and geothermal resource potential on the southern margin of the Junggar basin
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Junji Chen, Yingchun Wang, Haozhu Zhang, Yi Wang, Pengfei Chen, Guangzheng Jiang, Jie Hu
abstract: The existing heat flow measurement points in the southern margin of the Junggar Basin are unevenly distributed, with notable gaps in certain areas, resulting in insufficient spatial constraints on the regional geothermal field. Meanwhile, the deep temperature distribution remains poorly characterized and the genesis of geothermal systems has not yet to be fully elucidated. To address these issues, static well temperature data from 16 boreholes were collected and integrated with previously published rock thermophysical parameters to obtain 7 new high-quality terrestrial heat flow values, increasing the total number of measurement points from 31 to 38 and effectively filling the gaps in heat flow coverage. Building on these results, one-dimensional steady-state heat conduction equations were applied to calculate and analyze the planar distribution of the geothermal field at depths shallower than 2000 m, and a comprehensive assessment of geothermal resource potential was conducted in conjunction with regional geological data. The results show that the geothermal gradient ranges from 11.4 to 22.4 °C/km, with a mean of 17.8 ± 2.3 °C/km, and the terrestrial heat flow ranges from 23.4 to 44.5 mW/m², with a mean of 36.2 ± 4.7 mW/m². At burial depths of 500–2000 m, localized high-temperature thermal anomalies are identified in the Sikeshu Depression, the central Qigu Fault-Fold Belt, and the central Huomatu Anticline Belt, which are interpreted as local thermal anomaly zones on the southern margin of the Junggar Basin. The overall low heat flow background is primarily attributed to the combined effects of groundwater circulation, basement relief, structural configuration, and sedimentation rate. The total geothermal resources are estimated at 3823.6 × 10¹⁸ J, equivalent to 123.8 billion tons of standard coal; the Jurassic system contains the most abundant resources at 1066.1 × 10¹⁸ J, while the Quaternary and Neogene reservoirs have the least at 44.8 × 10¹⁸ J. The new heat flow data are consistent with previously published results, together corroborating the low geothermal background of the southern Junggar Basin. These findings provide an important reference for understanding the present-day geothermal field and for geothermal resource exploration and development in the study area.

title: Thermal conductivity evaluation using an integrated method: An example from the Horn River Basin, Canada
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Kezhen Hu, Wanju Yuan, Xiaojun Liu, Stephen E. Grasby, Zhuoheng Chen
abstract: The Horn River Basin in northeastern British Columbia, Canada, hosts significant unconventional shale-gas resources and geothermal potential within the Devonian Horn River Group (HRG). The organic-rich HRG shale is highly heterogeneous due to complex mineralogy and matrix variability across the basin, posing challenges for accurate thermal conductivity (TC) prediction. This study presents an integrated approach to evaluate spatial TC variability by combining comprehensive petrophysical characterization with two-phase mixing models: the Voigt–Reuss–Hill (VRH) average approach and the geometric mean (GM) method. Machine learning techniques were applied to extensive mineralogical data to predict mineral compositions from well logs, while total organic carbon (TOC), porosity, and fluid saturation were quantified through core–log calibrations and statistical analysis. TC profiles were then calculated using the VRH and GM models, incorporating calculated component volumes and mineral TC values adjusted for in situ temperature and pressure conditions. Both measured and modeled results indicate that TC in the low-porosity shale is predominantly controlled by mineralogy/lithology, increasing with quartz and carbonate content and decreasing with higher clay volume. Notably, the VRH approach performs better for lower TC values (<2.5 W/m·K) associated with higher clay and lower quartz and carbonate contents, whereas the GM method is more accurate at higher TC values (≥2.5 W/m·K), corresponding to lower clay and higher quartz and carbonate contents. Given the heterogeneous mineralogy and high TOC content of the HRG shale, integrating both models effectively captures the full range of TC variability and enhances predictive accuracy.

title: Integrated geothermometry for mixed-fluid carbonate geothermal systems under structural and hydrochemical constraints: Insights from the Yichuan Basin, central China
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Rudan Zheng, Gaoli Zhao, Jianhua Ping, Wei Leng, Joshua Mahwa, Jichang Zhao, Chengding Huo, Jiaqi Liu
abstract: Reliable characterization of reservoir temperature is an important step in geothermal resource evaluation, engineering design, and long-term utilization in sustainable subsurface energy systems. In groundwater-dominated geothermal systems hosted by fractured–vuggy carbonate reservoirs, conventional geothermometers often yield a wide range of temperature estimates owing to the combined effects of shallow groundwater mixing, re-equilibration, and hydrochemical buffering. These uncertainties hinder the interpretation of subsurface thermal regimes and groundwater circulation processes. In this study, we integrated hydrochemical indicators and environmental isotopes from the Yichuan Basin to constrain the fluid sources, circulation pathways, and mixing processes in a fault-controlled carbonate geothermal system. Building on hydrochemical and isotopic constraints on recharge, circulation, and mixing, we applied a multi-index-weighted geothermometer (MIWG) within a structure- and mixing-informed framework to estimate the reservoir temperatures in the Yichuan Basin. The results indicate that geothermal fluid evolution is jointly controlled by deep water–rock interactions and variable shallow groundwater mixing. Compared with individual geothermometers, the MIWG reduces the influence of method-specific extremes and yields more internally consistent well-specific temperature estimates. The MIWG-derived temperatures ranged from 78 to 157 °C across the study area, with the principal geothermal upflow system most plausibly concentrated at 128–157 °C. This study outlines a structure-informed interpretive framework for integrated geothermometry in mixed-fluid carbonate geothermal systems, distinguishing the indicative reservoir temperature range from the mixing-biased apparent temperatures. The proposed framework may help reduce the uncertainty in reservoir temperature assessment in structurally complex carbonate geothermal systems.

title: Reactive viscous fluid fracturing of volcanic rocks: Chemical weakening offsets viscosity-induced pressure increase
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Eko Pramudyo, Nagi Obata, Luis Salalá, Jiajie Wang, Noriaki Watanabe
abstract: Hydraulic stimulation of volcanic reservoirs can be hindered by strong fluid infiltration into pores, vesicles, and microfractures, which suppresses pressure build-up and limits the formation of conductive fractures. Increasing fluid viscosity can reduce fluid loss, but typically at the cost of higher fracturing pressure. Here, we tested whether this viscosity–pressure trade-off can be mitigated by combining viscosity control with chemical weakening of the rock matrix. Triaxial fracturing experiments were conducted at 180 °C on volcanic rocks using water-like fluids, non-reactive viscous fluids, and reactive viscous fluids composed of the biodegradable chelating agent N,N-bis(carboxymethyl)- L -glutamic acid (GLDA) and the biopolymer scleroglucan. Water-like fluids showed strong matrix infiltration and were ineffective at generating large-aperture fractures. Increasing viscosity suppressed infiltration and promoted wider fractures, but increased fracturing pressure. When GLDA was added to the viscous fluid, fracture aperture and fracture-network complexity increased further, while fracturing pressure in the benchmark andesitic tuff experiments remained comparable to that during water injection despite the much higher fluid viscosity. The results are consistent with chemically induced weakening offsetting the pressure increase normally associated with viscous fluids. Additional experiments on andesitic lava and rhyolitic reservoir rock suggest that reactive viscous fluids can also propagate pre-existing fractures and promote branching in volcanic rocks with contrasting pore structures. These findings highlight the potential of reactive viscous fluid fracturing as a low-pressure stimulation strategy for geothermal reservoirs, with possible relevance to proppant-less reservoir stimulation.

title: Potential assessment of critical raw materials from European geothermal fluids
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Laura Spitzmüller, Andrea Flores Salinas, Valentin Goldberg, Jens C. Grimmer, Rafael Villablanca-Ahues, Fabian Nitschke
abstract: The energy transition is accompanied by a growing demand for raw materials. The EU Critical Raw Materials Act (CRMA) foresees at least 10% of raw material supply covered by domestic sources. Geothermal fluids have the potential to contribute significantly achieving this target. Beyond the well-known and extensively studied lithium resources in European geothermal fluids, additional potential for other elements exists. We assess the potential of 64 elements in geothermal fluids that are defined as critical and strategic raw materials or raw materials in general under the CRMA. This assessment is based on >4000 geothermal fluid analyses across Europe. In summary, 13 of the 64 assessed elements are identified to provide the largest potential based on (a) their concentrations in geothermal fluids, (b) their ability to contribute to domestic supply and reduce supply-chain risks, (c) their hypothetical market value, and (d) their geostrategic importance. These elements are Li, B, Mg, Si, Mn, Ge, As, Rb, Sr, Cs and Pb with high reliability and Sc and Pd with low reliability. At the lower end of the spectrum are nine elements with the lowermost potentials (Se, Zr, Nb, In, Sn, Te, Ta, Re, Bi) and the Rare Earth Elements. Our evaluation framework simultaneously considers abundance and availability, economic potential and geostrategic and environmental aspects, thereby improving comparability across elements. Having identified these 13 promising candidates, future research can be more effectively focused on detailed resource assessments and the development of targeted extraction strategies.

title: Sustainable cementitious blends incorporating rice husk ash and silica flour for geothermal well applications
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Eduardo Lins, Rafael Ventura, Fabio Pereira, Rodrigo Santiago, Antonio Martinelli, Julio Freitas
abstract: Geothermal wells expose cement sheaths to temperatures up to 300 °C, where Class G cement slurries lose mechanical strength, compromising well integrity and long-term zonal isolation. To address this challenge, this study investigated the use of rice husk ash (RHA), a sustainable silica-rich material, combined with silica flour (SF) as a partial replacement for cement in cementitious mixtures designed for geothermal well conditions. Six cementitious systems with a constant slurry density of 15 ppg and varying RHA and SF contents were prepared and cured at 300 °C and 2000 psi for 7, 14, and 28 days. The hardened specimens were characterized by uniaxial compressive strength (UCS), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The results showed that RHA significantly improved mechanical performance, increasing compressive strength by up to 4 times compared with the standard slurry. Higher RHA contents also reduced strength retrogression and promoted denser microstructures after prolonged curing. XRD analyses revealed the predominance of thermally stable phases, particularly tobermorite and xonotlite, which contributed to enhanced mechanical stability. These findings demonstrate that cement systems incorporating RHA and silica flour have significant potential to mitigate strength retrogression and enhance the high-temperature performance of geothermal well cementing applications.

title: Hydrogeochemical processes and thermal mechanisms of deep-buried uplift dolostone reservoirs in the North China Basin
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Hankun Li, Jiexiang Li, Chuanxia Ruan, Zhilong Liu, Yun Chen, Feng Du
abstract: Deep-buried karst thermal reservoirs in large sedimentary basins, particularly those in the North China Basin, possess considerable exploitation and utilization potential. Within this basin, the Tianjin area constitutes a typical buried-uplift geothermal zone, where the deeply buried dolostone of the Wumishan Formation acts as the primary karst reservoir. Focusing on this reservoir, this study integrated hydrochemical analysis, environmental isotope analysis, and inverse hydrogeochemical modeling to investigate the circulation and evolution patterns of deep geothermal water, and to establish a conceptual model illustrating the heat accumulation and control mechanisms of the buried-uplift geothermal anomaly zone. The results indicate that the primary recharge source of the geothermal water is atmospheric precipitation in the northern Yanshan area, with no evidence of significant recharge from deeper high-temperature reservoir water. The geothermal fluids can be interpreted as leaching water derived from marine saline sedimentary rocks. Hydrochemically, the dominant water types are HCO3·Cl-Na and HCO3·SO4·Cl-Na. The hydrochemical composition is mainly controlled by host-rock leaching, carbonate precipitation, cation exchange, and sulfate reduction, with no evidence for significant mantle-derived inputs or magmatic degassing effects. Hydraulically, the Wumishan Formation exhibits favorable hydraulic connectivity across different tectonic units. The geothermal water generally flows from the northeast to the southwest, and locally migrates from the core of uplift zones toward both flanks. The degree of groundwater confinement increases progressively from the northeast to the southwest. The Shuangyao Uplift and Baitangkou Depression feature favorable groundwater flow conditions, whereas the Xiaohanzhuang Uplift serves as a groundwater stagnation zone. Collectively, the geothermal anomaly of the Tianjin buried uplift represents a “conduction-convection composite” geothermal system. Regional geothermal anomalies are primarily controlled by preferential conductive heat accumulation over basement uplifts and are locally influenced by groundwater convection within fault zones, while widespread intra-formational convection within the reservoir facilitates heat transfer and promotes reservoir temperature homogenization.

title: Field-validated thermodynamic assessment of hybrid gas-removal systems for geothermal power plants
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Suyanto, Triyogi Yuwono, Lina Agustina, Bambang Teguh Prasetyo, Budi Ismoyo
abstract: Non-condensable gas accumulation in geothermal condensers increases condenser pressure, raises turbine backpressure, and reduces steam expansion performance. Conventional steam jet ejector systems remove these gases but consume motive steam that would otherwise contribute to power generation. This study evaluates a hybrid gas-removal configuration combining a steam jet ejector and a liquid-ring vacuum pump using operational data from the Kamojang geothermal field, Indonesia. A steady-state thermodynamic model was developed in Engineering Equation Solver to integrate turbine expansion, condenser behaviour, gas-removal processes, cooling systems, and auxiliary power consumption into a unified mass and energy-balance framework. The model was validated against operational data from Kamojang Units 2–4, with deviations of <5% in the principal operating parameters. At a gross turbine output of 56 MW, the hybrid configuration reduced total steam demand from 398,520 to 392,760 kg/h, a reduction of 5760 kg/h (1.45%). The hybrid system required an additional 156.3 kW of liquid-ring vacuum pump power and produced a net output of 54,359 kW, compared with 54,513 kW for the conventional ejector system. Ejector outlet pressure was optimised using total power-penalty minimisation, with the minimum penalty occurring at approximately 0.33 bar abs. Parametric analysis showed lower specific steam consumption for the hybrid configuration at higher non-condensable gas concentration and condenser pressure. The hybrid configuration became economically favourable when steam cost exceeded USD 0.03614/kWh or non-condensable gas concentration exceeded 0.10185%. The results demonstrate the trade-off between reduced motive-steam consumption and increased auxiliary power demand in hybrid gas-removal systems.

title: Liquid nitrogen as a waterless fracturing fluid for enhanced geothermal systems: Mechanisms, challenges, and opportunities
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): C. Beddage, P.G. Ranjith, S.Q. Yang
abstract: Liquid nitrogen (LN₂) cryogenic fracturing has gained increasing attention as a waterless stimulation approach for Enhanced Geothermal Systems (EGS), offering a potential alternative to conventional hydraulic fracturing in high-temperature reservoirs. By inducing rapid thermal contraction, phase transition, and vapor pressurization, LN₂ can stimulate rock without the use of water or chemical additives, thereby reducing water demand and associated environmental constraints. This review summarizes recent advances (2024–2025) based on laboratory experiments, numerical modelling, and field experience from hydrocarbon reservoirs, noting that no full-scale geothermal LN₂ field trials have yet been reported. Laboratory studies show that LN₂ treatment can result in 13.6–76% reductions in compressive strength and up to 86% in tensile strength, three-to-five-fold increases in permeability, and up to 48% enhancement in fracture connectivity. Irreversible thermo-mechanical damage is consistently observed once reservoir temperatures exceed a critical transition window of 200–300 °C. Complementary thermo-hydro-mechanical damage models predict breakdown pressure reductions of 7.14–46.15%, in good agreement with experimental observations. These characteristics, lower fracture initiation pressures, increased fracture complexity, and substantial reduction or, in some cases, complete elimination of water use during fracture initiation, are particularly attractive for EGS development in arid and water restricted regions. Despite these advantages, important challenges remain, including cryogenic fluid handling, limited proppant transport capacity, uncertainties in long term fracture stability, and the absence of field scale geothermal validation. Future research should focus on pilot scale geothermal demonstrations, optimization of hybrid LN₂ assisted stimulation strategies, and comprehensive techno-economic assessment. LN₂ cryogenic fracturing represents a high potential, though not yet field proven, stimulation pathway for next generation geothermal energy development.

title: Tracing the source and evolution of organic matter in geothermal environments
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Val Maverick Abecia, Andrea Vieth-Hillebrand, Sonia Salah, Ben Laenen, Simona Regenspurg, Valérie Cappuyns
abstract: Despite recent advances in molecular characterization of organic matter in geothermal fluids, its origin, transformation processes, and physicochemical properties remain poorly understood. It can be assumed that dissolved organic matter (DOM) originates from the geothermal reservoir rocks (natural organic matter, NOM) and from anthropogenic additives such as scaling and corrosion inhibitors (synthetic organic matter, Synthetic OM) mixed with the geothermal fluid during operation. In this study, Liquid Chromatography-Organic Carbon Detection (LC-OCD) was used to characterize NOM and Synthetic OM contributions to the geothermal brine. NOM leachability from reservoir rocks was investigated by batch leaching experiments using 3.5 mol L − 1 NaCl at 125 °C and 70 °C. Synthetic OM contribution was assessed by studying the thermal degradation of three inhibitor types (acrylates, phosphonates, and a commercial inhibitor mixture) diluted in 3.5 mol L − 1 NaCl, also at 125 °C and 70 °C. The results show that the leachable NOM fraction (3%–10%) is primarily composed of hydrophilic low molecular weight organics and macromolecules, with minor hydrophobic components. Synthetic organics from antiscalants and chemical inhibitors degrade under high temperature and salinity conditions, releasing diverse organic molecules. They can form organic precipitates that may clog filters in geothermal installations when an inappropriate inhibitor is selected, thereby impairing geothermal plant operations. Comparison with organic matter in natural geothermal brines reveals that their molecular weight distribution is the same as that of NOM and Synthetic OM, with low molecular weight organics predominating. Characterizing commercial inhibitor mixtures remains challenging due to undisclosed formulations, as well as analytical limitations. Although low resolution chromatographic methods provide valuable information on compositional characteristics of DOM and on molecular weight distribution, they do not allow an unequivocal distinction between NOM and Synthetic OM, justifying the need for high resolution chromatographic techniques and other complementary analytical methods.

title: Geochemical dynamics and predictive modeling of water-rock interaction during geothermal reinjection in coal mine gobs
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Yuanyuan Jiang, Xincheng Hu, Jiawen Cai, Guangping Huang, Zhaoyang Yu, Chengkai Fan, Shengqiang Yang
abstract: Geothermal reinjection in mine gobs is a promising method for geothermal energy exploration, but the heat mining efficiency can be reduced by the corrosion or scaling within pipelines caused by water-rock interaction. To elucidate the hidden mechanism, we conducted constant-temperature oscillation and water quality experiments and then established partial least squares (PLS) prediction models for water-rock interaction development prediction. The hydrochemical classification showed that the hydrochemical type shifted from 18-A to 21-A attributing to mineral dissolution, precipitation, and cation exchange during reinjection. The self-organizing mapping (SOM) and ion-ratio analysis revealed that there were three major ion sources: carbonate, evaporite, and silicate dissolutions. Additionally, rock pore structure and saturation index (SI) analysis illustrated that mineral precipitation was the leading water-rock interaction process to the decline of ion concentrations (i.e., Na⁺, K+, Ca2+, Mg2+, Cl-, SO4 2-, HCO3 -). Notably, Chlor-alkali index (CAI) analysis revealed that positive cation exchange was the key geochemical process, leading to the abundance of Na⁺ and the depletion of Ca²⁺and Mg²⁺. The mean square errors and determination coefficients of the established SI and CAI prediction models illustrated that the prediction results accorded well with the experiment results, providing a feasible method to predict the development of water-rock interaction during geothermal reinjection in gobs.

title: Hydraulic fracturing experimental study of high temperature granite with water and supercritical carbon dioxide
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Zheng Jiang, Biao Shu, Yongpeng Hu, John McLennan
abstract: Geothermal energy is a clean and renewable energy resource that can help reduce carbon emissions. Supercritical carbon dioxide (ScCO2) has been proposed as a substitute for water in hydraulic fracturing of deep geothermal reservoirs, due to its unique physical properties. Laboratory hydraulic fracturing experiments using water and ScCO2 were conducted to compare their fracturing performance. The experiments were carried out at temperatures of 50, 150, and 250 °C, and the confining pressures of 5, 10, and 15 MPa, respectively. The results show the breakdown pressures of ScCO2 fracturing are about 15.0-48.6% lower than those of water fracturing. Analytical calculation of breakdown pressure shows that Hubbert and Willis model provides a reasonable estimate for water fracturing with an average percentage error of 13.3%, while modified Haimson and Fairhurst model, which considered pore pressure distribution, works better for ScCO2 fracturing with an average percentage error of 6.8%. The fractures generated by ScCO2 fracturing predominantly propagate along mineral grain boundaries, but those generated by water fracturing typically cut directly through mineral grains. In addition to a dominant fracture, ScCO2 fracturing generated an average of 6 secondary fractures, while water fracturing generated an average of only 1 secondary fracture. The number of secondary fractures in ScCO2 fracturing increases significantly with increasing temperature, from an average of 2 at 50 °C to 11 at 250 °C.

title: Experimental investigation on mitigating the thermal contact resistance at the soil - energy geo-structure interface
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Omar Elkezza, Mostafa Mohamed
abstract: Previous studies demonstrated the effectiveness of thermally enhanced backfill materials in improving borehole heat exchanger performance; however, limited experimental research studies exist on investigating the potential benefits of placing thermally enhanced soils at the soil-energy geo-structure interface to address and mitigate the thermal contact resistance. This paper presents results of a comprehensive experimental investigation on the use of thermally enhanced sands placed at the interface of energy geo-structures (EGS) such as piles and walls to improve heat transfer between energy geo-structures and the surrounding soils. The effectiveness of using of two different conductive additives named graphTHERM and carbon fibre in enhancing the thermal properties of sands was first evaluated. Subsequently, a series of tests using a relatively large-scale testing rig was performed to assess the influence of the thermally enhanced sand placed at the soil-EGS interface on the thermal performance of energy piles and walls during cooling. The results indicated that a 10% addition of graphTHERM and carbon fibres was an optimum level of additive improving the sand thermal conductivity by 62% and 35 % respectively. Placing a 100 mm of thermally enhanced sands by graphTHERM and carbon fibres at the interface between energy pile and surrounding soils was found highly effective in enhancing the heat transfer rate by 81 % and 54 % respectively. Furthermore, placing a 200 mm layer of thermally enhanced sands by graphTHERM and carbon fibres at the interface of energy walls increased the heat transfer rate by 108 % and 80 % respectively. The results demonstrated that the use of thermally enhanced sands at the soil-EGS interface was effective in expanding the thermally active soil zone without causing any increase in the lateral earth pressure acting on the EGS above those measured when the EGS was constructed in pure sand. The findings demonstrated the potential benefits of using thermally enhanced sands at the soil-EGS interface to improve heat exchange performance and contribute to the development of more efficient geo-energy systems.

title: Magnetotelluric evidence for a possible fault-guided fluid pathway beneath Tatapani hot springs in the Son-Narmada-Tapti lineament zone of Central India
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Prasanta K. Patro, Ujjal Borah, Khasi Raju, S. P. Eknath Rao, K. Chinna Reddy, S. Dhamodharan, S.V. S. Sarma
abstract: The geologically and structurally controlled geothermal activity of the Tatapani hot springs region, confined within an ENE-WSW trending Son-Narmada-Tapti lineament (SONATA) zone, has been investigated by magnetotelluric (MT) studies. MT is a crucial tool for identifying geothermal reservoirs as it is highly sensitive to variations in subsurface electrical conductivity, making it one of the most significant geophysical methods for exploring geothermal resources. The Tatapani geothermal region features shallow hot water aquifers hosted in highly porous formations, while the primary thermal reservoir lies at greater depths. A detailed three-dimensional inversion of MT data reveals an ENE–WSW–trending conductive zone (<20 Ω.m) aligned with the Tatapani Fault at shallow depths, transitioning to an approximately E–W trend between 2 and 6 km depth, interpreted as the main geothermal reservoir. This cone-shaped conductive body with a narrow apex near the surface and a broad base at ∼6 km depth indicates a tectonically guided up-flow zone. This geometry reflects ascending hydrothermal fluids along deep-seated fault intersections and fracture networks, with lateral expansion within a permeable granitic basement. Infiltrated meteoric water, mostly from the Gondwana Formation, convectively circulates within the Proterozoic basement of the Chota-Nagpur Gneissic Complex, where it is heated by anomalous geothermal gradients. The causative sources for the conductive anomalies in this region are likely associated with radiogenic heat generation from basement rocks, enhanced regional heat flow and enhanced permeability along reactivated faults.

title: Genesis of low-heat flow and topography-driven geothermal field regulation at the southwestern margin of the Huangling Dome, Yangtze Craton: Insights from borehole logging and coupled hydrothermal modeling
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Ziqiang Ren, Jiliang Wang, Heping Wu, Xiaoqiu Yang, Wenzhong Hao, Qi Xu, Du Liu, Long Tan, Peng Zhao
abstract: Accurate terrestrial heat flow determination is crucial for deciphering lithospheric thermal structure and deep dynamic processes. This assignment is particularly challenging in karst terrains with significant topographic relief, where groundwater flow driven by topography drastically reshapes shallow thermal regimes, obscuring deep-sourced heat flow signals. A direct consequence of this limitation is the persistent uncertainty in assessing the true thermal state of cratonic interiors. To address this, we conducted an integrated study at the southwestern margin of the Huangling Dome, Yangtze Craton. The overarching aim was to decouple the effects of hydrothermal circulation from the regional thermal state, thereby establishing a reliable background heat flow and quantifying the key mechanisms governing geothermal field heterogeneity. Through synthesis of borehole temperature logging, rock conductivity measurements, and coupled hydrothermal numerical modeling, we obtained measured heat flow values ranging from 18.1 to 40.4 mW/m². Our study concludes that values of 35.0∼40.4 mW/m² from nonsoluble rock areas robustly represent apparent regional background heat flow, which confirms the low heat flow characteristic of the study area relative to the continental average of China. Numerical simulations compellingly demonstrate that topography-driven groundwater forced convection, constituting the dominant mechanism and modulated by structural configuration and lithology, results in significant cooling and pronounced low heat flow anomalies within karst aquifers. Conversely, heat flow in nonsoluble rocks is governed by thermal refraction and lithological controls. These findings not only constrain the thermal state of the Yangtze Craton but also provide a generalized conceptual and methodological framework for reliably interpreting heat flow and assessing geothermal resources in other topographically complex terrains worldwide.

title: Reservoir response to long-term production in a low-enthalpy geothermal system: The Kızılcahamam field, Galatian volcanic province, Türkiye
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Elif Yilmaz Turali
abstract: The Kızılcahamam geothermal field in Central Anatolia (Türkiye–Ankara), hosted within the Galatian Volcanic Province, has been exploited for district heating and thermal tourism since the mid-1990s. Measured production temperatures reach up to 86 °C across the field. This study integrates temperature–depth logs, water-level observations, and hydrogeochemical records to evaluate the reservoir’s thermal, hydraulic, and chemical evolution under nearly two decades of production with intermittent reinjection. Temperature–depth profiles and a 3D interpolated model reveal vertically heterogeneous gradients and convective upflow aligned with NE–SW and N–S fault systems. Water-level data combined with net extraction estimates indicate progressive depressurization, spatially variable drawdown, and heterogeneous storage behavior associated with structurally controlled flow pathways. Hydrochemical data show a temporal shift from Na–HCO₃ to Na–Cl water types, expressed by decreasing bicarbonate, increasing chloride, elevated Cl/B ratios, and strengthened reverse ion-exchange signatures—features that collectively suggest reduced shallow recharge and a relative increase in deeper, chemically evolved fluid contributions, particularly after reinjection ceased in 2011. However, bottom-hole temperature records indicate no systematic spatial or temporal increase in reservoir enthalpy despite progressive pressure decline and hydrochemical shifts. The integrated thermal, hydraulic, and geochemical evidence supports a conceptual model in which long-term production appears to favor structurally controlled deep flow while progressively reducing shallow contributions. As the analysis relies primarily on long-term monitoring records and empirical storage approximations rather than fully coupled dynamic reservoir modeling, the results should be interpreted as first-order system-scale assessments. These findings highlight the need for continuous monitoring and improved reinjection practices to ensure the sustainable management of low- to medium-enthalpy volcanic geothermal systems such as Kızılcahamam.

title: Hydrothermal system of the Middle Atlas (Morocco): Hydrochemistry, structural controls, and emplacement model
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): El Mehdi Jeddi, Ahmed Ntarmouchant, Maria do Rosário Carvalho, Telmo M. Bento dos Santos, Mohamed Lahtani, Brahim Mali, Salma Zerouali Masror, Nahla Ntarmouchant, Mustapha Elabouyi, My Hachem Smaili, Ayman Agharabi, Ikrame Allaoui, Youssef Driouch, Eduardo Anselmo Ferreira da Silva
abstract: Morocco's Middle Atlas offers remarkable hydro-geothermal potential through a multitude of thermal resurgences closely associated with deep regional tectonic structures, particularly the Northern, Central, and Southern Middle Atlas faults, forming a complex NE-SW-oriented structural corridor. A multidisciplinary study was conducted on eight selected thermal springs emerging along these structures, with temperatures ranging from 19 to 53.5 °C and pH values between 6.0 and 7.3. Hydrochemical analysis reveals two distinct water facies: i) Na-Cl type evolving within relatively closed hydrothermal systems sealed by impermeable marls, thereby preserving their deep geochemical signatures, and ii) Ca-HCO3 type developing in open systems within fractured limestones, where dilution by surface infiltration is favored. These results highlight the fluid circulation and interaction with reservoirs of diverse lithological nature connected by fracture networks, including Paleozoic crystalline basement, Triassic and Miocene evaporitic formations, and Jurassic carbonates. Geochemical modelling reveals that these thermal waters are oversaturated with carbonate minerals, a result of their equilibration within the Jurassic carbonate reservoir before their discharge to the surface, while their oversaturation in mafic and ultramafic minerals, as well as their concentrations of trace and rare earth elements, indicate their circulation at depth in the volcanic hydrothermal systems identified in the Middle Atlas basement. Na-Cl waters are characterised by their oversaturation in silicate and clay minerals resulting from their interaction with the Paleozoic crystalline basement. The indications provided by these waters are confirmed by the IIRG reservoir classification method. Geothermometry indicates reservoirs equilibrium temperatures between 80 and 137 °C and circulation depths from 1.9 to 3.5 km. Stable isotopic signatures (δ18O: -9.08 to -6.68‰ and δ2H: -64.3 to -37.9‰) confirm a meteoric origin of the fluids, with recharge areas located in the SW part of the Middle Atlas at elevations estimated between 1513 and 2337 m. Structural analysis shows that these thermal springs emerge at the intersection of the NE-SW and E-W to NW-SE fault systems. The NE-SW faults facilitate fluid flow from the southwestern recharge zones to the northeastern discharge zones, while the E-W to NW-SE faults correspond to thrusts and faults sealed by Triassic clays that block lateral flow and promote the vertical ascent of fluids to the surface. Thus, this study characterizes the Middle Atlas hydrothermal system as a large-scale, fault-controlled geothermal province, highlighting its considerable potential for sustainable energy development.

title: Optimization of well patterns for heat recovery in sedimentary geothermal systems: A hybrid GRA-COBRA approach
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Jun Xie, Shuxing Mu, Yuxuan Liu
abstract: Engineering parameters of enhanced geothermal systems (EGS) directly govern heat recovery performance and economic viability. To address the practical engineering challenge of selecting the most robust well configuration amidst conflicting technical and economic objectives, this study develops a comprehensive evaluation and decision-making framework tailored for sedimentary geothermal systems. First, a 3D discrete fracture network model is established to simulate the thermal extraction behavior of six distinct well patterns. These configurations are evaluated through a multi-dimensional index system comprising production temperature, power generation, total heat extraction, flow impedance, and cost of electricity (COE). To systematically identify the optimal well pattern, a balance must be struck among these conflicting criteria. Consequently, we introduce a novel multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) method, GRA-COBRA, which employs a cooperative game model for weight determination and integrates Grey Relational Analysis (GRA) with Comprehensive Distance-Based Ranking (COBRA) for evaluation. Application of the GRA-COBRA methodology identifies the single-injection-triple-production (1I3P) pattern as the optimal configuration, achieving the best equilibrium between energy output and economic feasibility. Finally, comparative analysis and sensitivity tests confirm that the proposed framework provides project developers with a more rational and robust decision-making tool compared to traditional methods.

title: Dual-porosity numerical modeling and probabilistic resource assessment of the Ulumbu geothermal field, Flores, Indonesia
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Idrissa Abalhassan Jaha, Tubagus Ahmad Fauzi Soelaiman, Zuher Syihab, Ali Ashat, Tony Widiatmoro, M. Burhanuddin Aulia Asy’ari
abstract: Sustainable geothermal development requires reliable forecasts of reservoir performance and recoverable energy potential. Numerical reservoir simulation is an effective approach to achieve this, but its reliability depends on accurate calibration and quantifying uncertainties in key reservoir parameters that strongly influence power potential estimation. Accordingly, this study develops the first dual-porosity numerical model of the steam capped Ulumbu geothermal field, fully calibrated to both natural-state conditions and production history using the updated 2023 conceptual model, and applies an integrated Experimental Design-Response Surface Methodology-Monte Carlo (ED-RSM-MC) workflow to assess the probabilistic impact of reservoir-parameter uncertainty on long-term generation capacity. A three-dimensional model was developed using the TOUGH2 simulator, integrating geological, geochemical, geophysical, and well data. Calibration against pressure–temperature profiles from wells ULB-1, ULB-2, and ULB-3 yielded RMSE values of 1.9–7.1°C and 3.1–8.5 bar, successfully reproducing natural-state behavior. The close agreement between simulated and observed pressures indicates that the model represents reservoir connectivity and permeability structure realistically. Five key uncertain parameters; matrix porosity, matrix permeability, fracture volume factor, liquid saturation, and fracture spacing were systematically varied using a Box–Behnken design to construct a response surface model. The resulting proxy model, combined with Monte Carlo simulation, produced a most-likely (P50) power-potential estimate of 71.59 MW over a 30-year production period. Matrix porosity and matrix permeability were the most influential parameters controlling power output. Overall, the integrated modelling–statistical framework provides a physically consistent and probabilistically robust basis for sustainable development planning of the Ulumbu geothermal field.

title: Advancing geothermal reservoir temperature prediction in the Western Anatolia (Türkiye) using synthetic hydrogeochemical data from rank–Gaussian copulas
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Füsun S. Tut Haklidir, Mehmet Haklidir
abstract: Data-driven geothermal reservoir temperature prediction can complement classical geothermometer applications in geothermal provinces with high resource potential, such as Western Anatolia (Türkiye). However, the limited availability and heterogeneous nature of hydrogeochemical datasets constrain the use of high-capacity machine-learning models and weaken their generalization to new prospective fields. In this study, a rank-Gauss copula (RGC) based synthetic data generation framework is proposed to learn the joint dependence structure among routinely measured hydrogeochemical variables and generate additional samples consistent with the observed distributions. Using a benchmark dataset of 83 hot springs and geothermal wells alongside seven commonly measured variables (pH, EC, K+, Na+, Btotal, SiO2, and Cl-), the generated synthetic data closely matched the real data’s marginal behavior and multivariate relationships (average two-sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistic approximately 0.04 across variables), while preserving key field-consistent correlation patterns. Two predictive settings for reservoir temperature prediction were evaluated in the study: (i) a deep neural network (DNN) ensemble pre-trained on RGC-synthetic data and fine-tuned on real samples, and (ii) NGBoost models trained on real-only versus real-plus-RGC data and test performance was consistently improved by RGC augmentation. Overall, the proposed RGC framework is data-driven, model-independent, and straightforward to implement; the Western Anatolia (Türkiye) is used as a case study, and the approach is intended to be transferable to geothermal provinces with high resource potential where routine hydrogeochemical analyses are available but reliable reservoir temperature measurements are scarce, enabling the generation of realistic synthetic datasets and improving the robustness and generalization of reservoir temperature estimation.

title: Unraveling the fluid origin, circulation and heat sources of the fault-controlled Santa Teresita Geothermal System (Pipanaco basin, NW Argentina): insights from hydrochemical, isotopic and structural analysis
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Gimena M. Uran, Mariano A. Larrovere, Verena A. Campodonico, Pablo H. Alasino
abstract: The southern sector of the Pipanaco basin in NW Argentina (Eastern Sierras Pampeanas) was studied in order to comprehend its geothermal system. This study presents new detailed isotopic and hydrogeochemical data, together with a geological-structural analysis. A new comprehensive conceptual model for the Santa Teresita Geothermal System (STGS) is proposed, highlighting the role of the regional fault-system. The thermal waters of the STGS have a Na+-SO4 2−-Cl− composition, evidencing a gradual mineralization increase in the groundwater flow direction. The 222Rn concentrations measured in groundwater are consistent with waters contained in granitic fractured rocks. The stable isotopes indicate a meteoric origin with no evidence of mixing with magmatic waters. The study area presents a strong structural control over the thermal manifestations, and these are mainly concentrated on the intersection of two regional structures: the Villa Mervil – Santa Teresita reverse fault (NE-SW direction) and a dextral strike-slip fault (NNW-SSE direction). Neotectonic activity favored the development of high-permeability pathways, promoting the rise of thermal waters. The STGS corresponds to a low enthalpy geothermal system, with waters heated by the regional geothermal gradient and estimated reservoir temperatures in the range from 85 to 115 °C. It constitutes a geothermal system in the active contractional Andean broken foreland, with a reservoir depth that must exceed 3 km considering a geothermal gradient of ∼ 30 °C km−1. This study provides a robust model for future research on the geothermal potential of the region.

title: Influence of fluid-rock interactions on mechanical, thermal and transport properties of sandstone reservoir during geothermal waste fluid reinjection
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Jieqin Xia, Hong Tian, Sadiq J. Zarrouk, Eylem Kaya, Jun Zheng, Bin Dou, Yan Qin, Yanting Zhao, Sen Zhang
abstract: The Guantao formation sandstone geothermal reservoir (SGR) suffers from low reinjection efficiency, severely limiting its sustainable utilization. Reinjection of geothermal waste fluid (GF) back into the SGR triggers intense fluid-rock interactions (FRIs) driven by the coupled effects of mechanical stress, mineralogical composition, and the injected fluid’s physicochemical properties. In this study, we conducted core-scale reactor experiments (25 days) and a batch numerical model (360 days) consistent with experimental parameters to explore the FRI and its influence on rock mechanical, thermal, and transport properties. Results showed that during the initial 25 days, the rock mass loss rate, diameter increase rate, and porosity all exhibited a trend of first increasing and then decreasing. Thermal conductivity varied inversely with porosity, whereas permeability declined sharply within the first 5 hours, then increased, and then declined again. The peak strength and elastic modulus of the rocks showed a fluctuating trend, initially decreasing and then increasing. The combined experimental and simulation results revealed that, before 90 days, the evolution of porosity and permeability was primarily controlled by feldspar dissolution, clay precipitation, and secondary calcite formation. Then, the FRI system gradually approached chemical equilibrium. Building upon the core scale results, a THC-coupled Near-Wellbore model was developed using well-logging data and reinjection conditions. The simulation predicted that after 50 years, reinjection of GF induced a permeability-damaged zone in the near-well region extended to approximately 50 m, while the porosity-affected zone extended to about 100 m. These findings provide valuable engineering insights for similar SGR reinjection operations.

title: Preliminary Assessment of CO 2 Compression Behavior Modified by [BMIM][AlCl 4 ] for Engineered Geothermal Working Fluids
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Damian Janiga, Paweł Wojnarowski
abstract: Closed-loop geothermal systems (CLGS) benefit from engineered working fluids, and supercritical CO2 is a leading candidate due to its low viscosity and buoyancy-driven circulation. However, system performance depends sensitively on CO2 compressibility and behavior near the critical region. Ionic fluids (IFs) offer a potential route to tuning these properties, yet their interaction with CO2 under geothermal high-temperature, high-pressure (HTHP) conditions is not well understood. This study examines the mixing behavior of [BMIM][AlCl4] with CO2 using constant composition compression experiments at 30, 50 and 100 °C up to 25 MPa. The results show that [BMIM][AlCl4] alters CO2 thermodynamic response: mixtures retain substantially higher volume, near-critical compressibility peaks are strongly suppressed, and gas-like fluid-like crossover pressures shift upward. Volume-matching analysis reveals CO2 dissolution into the IF and microstructural reorganization of the halometallate phase. These findings demonstrate that [BMIM][AlCl4] acts as an active thermodynamic modifier rather than an inert additive. For geothermal applications, such IF-induced stiffening and fluctuation suppression could affect density control, circulation stability, and heat-extraction performance in CO2-based CLGS. The results provide foundational data for designing IF-CO2 working fluids tailored for next-generation geothermal systems.

title: Nigorikawa and Otake – Pioneering geothermal binary plants in Japan: Historical perspective, performance assessment, and lessons learned
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Ronald DiPippo
abstract: In the 1970′s in the wake of two Oil Shocks, the countries of the world began a quest for indigenous sources of energy. In particular, alternative means were sought to generate electricity without the need to burn fossil fuels. Japan started its Sunshine Program and included, among several technologies, geothermal energy of which their country has an abundance of potential. Two pilot geothermal binary power plants were created conceptually, designed, and built at locations at opposite ends of the country, and tested for a year. These plants, the Nigorikawa and Otake pilot plants, pioneered some of the features now common at binary plants that have spread across the world, but the technical details of these plants have not yet been published in the mainstream literature. This article describes the plants in technical detail, including their locations, assesses the test results on the basis of thermodynamic First Law and Second Law principles (including exergy), and discusses the implications for future plants. As test plants, their economics was not a priority and this article does not address that facet of the projects.

title: Conceptual model of the low-temperature geothermal system in the Cuenca Alta del Río Laja basin, Central Mexico
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Lucía Magali Ramírez-González, María Jesús Puy-Alquiza, Yanmei Li, Rosa María Prol-Ledesma, Jesús Horacio Hernández-Anguiano, Yasmin Hernández-Aburto, Diego Ruiz-Aguilar, Gabriela Ana Zanor, Raúl Miranda-Avilés, Viridiana Piña-González, Ashley V. Aguilar
abstract: Thermal waters in the Cuenca Alta del Río Laja are discharged from agricultural, public and recreational wells at temperatures from ∼29 to 47 °C. In this study we reviewed available surface and sub-surface information; the compilation includes geological, hydrogeological, hydrogeochemical, and geophysical data that were integrated into four cross-sections that constitute the first geothermal conceptual model of the basin. It is proposed that the heat source is driven by convection due to two main mechanisms: 1) deep convection controlled by the regional system of N-S and NW-SE normal faults; and 2) induced convection by pumping. Groundwater flows towards the center of the basin where thermal waters are sodium-bicarbonate type and they are mixed with shallower groundwater at lower temperature. Geothermometry allowed us to conceptualize the 102 °C isotherm; its position is only schematic and it is shallower in the fault zones due to convection. This study discusses the occurrence of a NW-SE buried fault and gives evidence that supports that at depth, the regional fault system enhances the vertical permeability and controls convection. We also discussed the occurrence of thermal samples unrelated to faults that may be associated to the water table drawdown as a result of overexploitation. This study has regional impact for groundwater management and geothermal exploration.

title: Field to laboratory assessment of subsurface thermal conductivity: A geothermal case study in Slovenia
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Karlo Borko, Fiona M. Chapman, Jasmin Raymond, Grzegorz Ryżyński, Nina Rman
abstract: Reliable characterization of subsurface thermal properties is essential for designing efficient shallow geothermal systems and assessing the potential of Ground Source Heat Pump and Underground Thermal Energy Storage systems. The objective of this study is to evaluate the reliability of thermal conductivity estimations from different approaches by comparing three in situ methods - conventional Thermal Response Test (TRT), Enhanced Thermal Response Test (ETRT), and Distributed Thermal Response Test (DTRT) - against each other and laboratory measurements on core samples. The tests were conducted in a 100 m deep borehole heat exchanger in the Krško Basin, Slovenia. Laboratory measurements employed needle probes and an optical Thermal Conductivity Scanner (TCS), while in situ testing utilized fibre-optic Distributed Temperature Sensing (DTS) for high-resolution temperature profiling. Results show that needle probe measurements consistently underestimate thermal conductivity relative to TCS- and DTS-based methods, by 22% to 48%, mainly due to sample desaturation and limited probe contact. DTS-based ETRT revealed vertical variations and groundwater-flow-influenced zones. Cemented fibre-optic cables introduced greater uncertainty and yielded 44% higher conductivities than the ETRT with the composite cable. TCS yielded thermal conductivities most consistent with in situ measurements while providing a favourable balance of time, cost, and reliability of results.

title: Detecting and characterizing a hidden geothermal system in the Mt. Endut area, Indonesia, through integrated soil-gas component analyses
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Mochamad Iqbal, Taiki Kubo, Koki Kashiwaya, Katsuaki Koike
abstract: A hidden geothermal system (HGS) is a specific, complex geothermal system that does not have surface thermal manifestations but has significant potential for energy resources. Despite the difficulty of exploration of such systems because of their concealed features, detection and development of these systems can significantly contribute to increasing geothermal power generation. This study aimed to detect and characterize an HGS in the Mt. Endut area, Banten, west Indonesia, and to clarify its relationship with the adjacent, conventional medium-temperature Cikawah Geothermal System (CGS). Mt. Endut area is classified as a hidden system because a thick low-permeability cap rock and sealed fault segments suppress surface discharge, with no evidence of a depressed water table or an overlying cold aquifer. Under such sealing conditions, moderately low-solubility CO2 and short-lived radon isotopes (222Rn and 220Rn) can migrate upward through minor fractures while liquid flow remains impeded, making them effective tracers of concealed fluid pathways. To evaluate this mechanism, an integrated soil-gas geochemical approach was employed, combining CO2 flux, δ13C-CO2, and radon isotopes measurements with interpretations from existing geophysical datasets, a complete Bouguer anomaly (CBA) map, and magnetotelluric (MT) data. The soil-gas survey revealed large variabilities in the CO2 flux (15 to 1399 g m − 2 day−1) and δ13C-CO2 (−18.71 to −9.75‰) caused by a complex mixture of biogenic and hydrothermal gas sources. The locations of high-flux zones of hydrothermal-dominated mixture (HDM) CO2 were strongly correlated with the Handeleum dextral fault having a permeable structure. The 222Rn/220Rn ratio was effective for differentiating gas source depths and attributing deep-seated 222Rn anomalies to major fault zones and advective transport. A key finding was the role of the NNE–SSW Endut normal fault as a distinct structural boundary separating the Endut HGS from the CGS, supported by a coincident gravity low and a steep MT resistivity gradient. Moreover, the results suggest that the two systems are driven by distinct heat sources, a deep magmatic body for the Endut HGS and a shallower andesitic intrusion for the CGS, and delineate three new potential areas warranting future exploration. Consequently, this study identifies robust geochemical signatures for both the concealed and conventional geothermal systems by high CO2 flux of HDM origin coexisting with shallow-source 222Rn, and underscores the effectiveness of this integrated approach in reducing exploration uncertainty for HGS detection and characterization. These result can contribute to the development of geothermal resources in Indonesia and other volcanic areas.

title: Hydraulic analysis of the GEOREAL fluid injection experiment at the KTB pilot hole, Germany
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): C.M. Boese, J. Kück, G. Zimmermann, G. Dresen, S. Kamrani, U. Harms, I. Sass, M. Bohnhoff
abstract: A total of 600 m 3 of fresh water was injected into the 4 km-deep KTB pilot borehole near Windischeschenbach, Germany, in November 2023. The main goal of the GEOREAL hydraulic stimulation experiment was to stimulate fractured metamorphic rocks in the vicinity of the well-characterised SE2 fault zone at 4 km depth with high flow rates and to compare rock and fluid responses to a previous one-year-long injection experiment in 2004/5 into the same formation. The intention was to quantify the potential for heat extraction at a site where temperature and pressure conditions are representative for crystalline rocks for large parts of Germany. Due to an unforeseen incident during packer deployment, however, a reduced fluid volume of 600 m 3 was injected, pressurising the entire pilot hole (KTB-VB), including the cased section to 3.85 km depth and the 150 m open borehole section below. Flow rates were variable ranging from 10 to 220 l/min. Pressure records were obtained at the well heads of KTB-VB and the main borehole (KTB-HB) at 200 m lateral distance at the surface which was also used for downhole microseismic monitoring. Hydraulic data were analysed and compared to results from 2004/5. The hydraulic parameters show similar values as in 2004/5 when no packer was blocking the borehole. Due to an unknown leak in the casing cement of the 35-year-old KTB-VB, the GEOREAL experiment had to be stopped earlier than planned. No microseismic events were detected during the injection using conventional event-detection methods. Hydraulic results for the KTB-VB injections two decades apart suggest that no significant permeability changes have occurred in the SE2 fault zone indicating that fracture healing does not play a major role in the reservoir. The pressure recordings from the KTB-HB showed no change caused by the injection into the KTB-VB, suggesting that either the injected volume was too small to cause a hydraulic response, too much fluid leaked into the formation, the hydraulic connection observed previously ceased to exist, its geometry is unfavourable for this configuration, or hydraulic diffusivity is smaller than suggested for previous experiments.

title: In-situ mechanical factors affecting hydraulic stimulation for deep-direct use heat extraction in Cambrian-Ordovician Potsdam and Beekmantown Group formations
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Sean A. Fulcher, Vishesh Bhadariya, Hunjoo P. Lee, Lawrence Cathles
abstract: Heat extraction in an Enhanced Geothermal System (EGS) requires uniformly distributed fluid pathways between parallel wells. Creating uniform flow by hydraulic fracturing in low-porosity, low-permeability formations remains challenging. Bedding planes, natural fractures, and trace fossil facies are potential geomechanical barriers to hydraulic fracture propagation in the Cambrian-Ordovician age Potsdam and Beekmantown Groups of the northern Appalachian Basin where Cornell University is investigating the feasibility of deep direct use (DDU) parallel well geothermal energy extraction. To better understand these geomechanical barriers, we subjected a suite of Potsdam and Beekmantown Group outcrop samples to semi-circular bend (SCB) tests, unconfined compression strength (UCS) tests, digital image correlation (DIC) strain field mapping, and microstructure analysis. Results show Mode I fracture propagation and fracture diversion is influenced by strain concentrations in natural fractures where fracture fill transitions from full to partially infilled. Interbedded dolostone-sandstone layers do not influence fracture trajectory because the mechanical contrast between dolostone and sandstone is low, and the interface is gradational and strongly cemented. Strain mapping indicates trace fossils produce strain anisotropy during loading in the samples, but this strain anisotropy consolidates at peak load and therefore does not affect fracture propagation.

title: Insights into the formation of a low heat flow geothermal system: integrated geochemical and geophysical evidence from Anjiazhuang, China
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Weizun Zhang, Yuanzhi Cheng, Meng Wang, Hui Zou, Liang Qie, Yizhuo Dong, Xiaoxiao Zhang, Jing Wang, Shuyang Wang, Qitao Ding, Jiabin Duan, Yulie Gong, Yanlong Kong
abstract: Low heat flow depressions are generally considered unfavorable for the development of shallow hydrothermal geothermal resources. However, this study identifies a promising shallow medium-low temperature geothermal resource within the boundary of the Dawenkou Basin.
