These findings deepen the understanding of isotopic variation and fractionation processes of evaporating water bodies in humid subtropical regions.

title: Navigating the energy-ecology-carbon nexus: A multi-objective reservoir operation framework for greener hydropower development
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Zhenxiang Xing, Pengyu Shi, Han Zhang, Yue Guan, Wenlong Tang, Yuanyang Li, Yinan Wang
abstract: Study Region The Nirji Reservoir is located in the Nenjiang River Basin, Northeast China. Study Focus Navigating the energy–ecology–carbon nexus is a critical challenge for the sustainable development of hydropower under China’s dual-carbon strategy. The failure of carbon emission mitigation by traditional reservoir operations has led to a shift in reservoirs from being carbon sinks to carbon sources and the deterioration of ecological performance. To address this issue, this study proposes a hydropower generation–ecology–low-carbon coordinated multi-objective reservoir operation framework (HECC-RO) that integrates inflow forecasting, carbon-emission accounting, Pareto-based multi-objective optimization, and multi-criteria decision analysis to evaluate alternative operation schemes under different management preferences. New Hydrological Insights Results show that the proposed framework improves the balance among hydropower generation, ecological performance, and carbon reduction in the Nirji Reservoir. Relative to the current engineering-practice baseline, the Carbon-optimal scheme reduces carbon emissions by 29.6% and EcoDev by 85.9%, with only a 12.3% loss in hydropower generation, and CEI decreases to 115–125 g/kWh. These findings provide regional hydrological insight into how monthly operation of a large upstream control reservoir in the Nenjiang River Basin can better coordinate hydropower production, downstream flow regulation, and low-carbon performance.

title: Using geochemical signatures to identify subsurface flow pathways in the intermittent reach of the Yusheng Creek in Taiwan
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Tsung-Yu Lee, Hsiu-Hao Yeh, Yen-Wei Pan, Shao-Yu Hsu, Yung-Chia Chiu, Jr-Chuan Huang
abstract: Study region Yusheng Creek is a mountain stream in central Taiwan where the critically endangered Formosan landlocked salmon (Oncorhynchus masou formosanus) has been reintroduced but remains vulnerable to intermittent streamflow. Study focus Subsurface flow pathways and groundwater-stream interactions were investigated using end-member mixing analysis (EMMA). Monthly water samples were collected from four observation wells, stream water, and tributaries during two monitoring periods (January–November 2017; October 2021–August 2022). Geochemical parameters and stable isotopes (δ¹⁸O and δ²H) were analyzed to trace water sources. New hydrological insights Results reveal contrasting hydrological connectivity between dry and wet years. During dry years, the hyporheic zone persisted within the streambed but remained disconnected from groundwater, while upstream stream water infiltrated and migrated downstream through subsurface pathways. In wet years, the hyporheic zone and groundwater formed a hydraulically connected system, as indicated by similar geochemical signatures. These results highlight the critical role of the hyporheic zone in maintaining longitudinal connectivity in intermittent mountain streams, providing new insights into subsurface flow dynamics in humid subtropical regions.

title: Contributions and driving factors of multi-pathway nutrient loss from gully slope of the Loess Plateau
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Lili Wang, Guanghui Zhang, Qingfeng Chen, Pingzong Zhu, Lin Liu
abstract: Study region This research was carried out in the Zhifanggou small watershed on the Chinese Loess Plateau. Gully slopes in this area feature fragile ecological condition and serve as the primary source of soil erosion and nutrient loss. Study focus Clarifying multi-pathway nutrient loss characteristics is essential for soil erosion and nutrient management. Current research lacks systematic understanding of the contribution and driving mechanisms of multi-pathway nutrient loss on gully slopes. So we conducted a comprehensive study based on eight natural rainfall events in 2021. Runoff plots (3 m × 1 m) were installed on six typical plant communities and one bare land (BL), to monitor carbon (C), nitrogen (N), and phosphorus (P) losses via runoff, sediment and litter export pathway, and key environmental factors were quantified. New hydrological insights for the region Plant communities produced runoff, sediment yield, and litter export mass ranges of 1.94–7.31 L m-², 2.57–5.18 g m-², and 0.26–0.78 g m-², respectively. Grasslands had higher C, N and P losses through runoff and sediment than shrublands, and litter-related nutrient losses in grasslands ranked as AG > CL > AS > BI. Sediment was the dominant nutrient loss pathway for BL, while shrublands mainly lost nutrients via litter export (43.66%-84.76%) rather than sediment pathway (3.85%-14.36%). Dominant nutrient loss pathways differed greatly among grassland communities. Soil total carbon (STC) and soil organic carbon (SOC) content significantly inhibited sediment-mediated C, N, and P loss (p < 0.05), while STC content significantly enhancing litter-mediated total C and P loss (p < 0.05). Runoff reduced nutrient loss via runoff and litter pathways, while significantly promoted sediment-mediated C, N, and P loss (p < 0.05). Overall, grassland communities exhibited better performance in reducing total nutrient loss across all three pathways. Soil surface carbon content and runoff were the main drivers of the loss pathways. The findings provide critical insights for designing soil conservation and nutrient loss control strategies.

title: Projecting 21st-century glacier change in the Qilian Mountains: A dynamic modeling approach of Laohugou Glacier No.12 with Elmer/Ice and CMIP6
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Yushuo Liu, Xiang Qin, Yuzhe Wang, Zizhen Jin, Jiawen Ren
abstract: Study region The Laohugou Glacier No.12 (LHG12) located at the west Qilian Mountains. Study focus Glaciers in the Qilian Mountains constitute a critical freshwater reservoir for the Hexi Corridor. In recent decades, their accelerated retreat has introduced new challenges to water resource applications downstream. As the largest valley glacier in the region, LHG12 holds considerable significance. However, dynamical modeling studies targeting this glacier remain limited and require further development. This study employs the Elmer/Ice model to perform a 3-D dynamical simulation of LHG12. Using measured ice thickness data as primary input, diagnostic simulations were conducted. Subsequently, AWS and downscaled CMIP6 data were used to project the evolution of LHG12 up to 2100 CE under the current climate baseline, the SSP1–2.6 and the SSP5–8.5 scenarios. New hydrological insights for the region The simulation results indicate a maximum basal temperature of −0.7 ℃, which is consistent with observations, suggesting that the base of LHG12 at surface elevations below 4 500 m a.s.l. is at or near the pressure melting point. Under the current baseline climate, the SSP1–2.6 and the SSP5–8.5 scenarios, the eastern and western branches of LHG12 are projected to separate around 2085 CE, 2069 CE and 2058 CE, respectively; by 2100 CE, the glacier area reduces by 6.33%, 10.68% and 59.17%, respectively; and the glacier volume decrease by 11.70%, 37.13% and 82.30%, respectively.

title: Salinity effects on water surface and phreatic evaporation in arid regions: Evidence from controlled experiments
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Mi Lei, Yanfeng Liu, Jinlong Zhou, Zixuan Qi, Ruiliang Jia
abstract: Study region Changji Groundwater Balance Experiment Station, located on the northern foothills of the Tianshan Mountains in Xinjiang, China. Study focus Evaporation from high-salinity water and shallow groundwater was investigated through controlled experiments across a TDS gradient (0.8–250 g·L⁻¹), groundwater depths (0.5, 1.0, and 3.0 m), and vadose-zone lithologies (fine sand and silty clay). Salinity suppressed water-surface evaporation following a negative exponential relationship, with inhibition rates ranging from 6.4% to 37.4%. For phreatic evaporation, higher salinity reduced evaporative flux, particularly at shallow depths (0.5 and 1.0 m). During the freezing period, freezing-point depression and snow insulation enhanced evaporation under saline conditions, whereas non-freezing periods showed consistent suppression. New hydrological insight A critical salinity threshold (TDS=30 g·L⁻¹) was identified where osmotic potential reversed, shifting from evaporation promotion to inhibition. Conversion coefficients for water-surface evaporation (Kₛ) and phreatic evaporation (Kₘ), and an evaporation response coefficient (R=1 −K) were established to facilitate estimation of saline evaporation from freshwater data. Additionally, a capillary rise limit in fine sand (<3.0 m) was revealed, and high salinity was demonstrated to sustain evaporative flux during freezing by overcoming ice‑barrier blockage. These findings suggest a revision to the traditional view that evaporation in deep, frozen zones is negligible and could provide practical tools for water-salt management in saline-affected agricultural regions.

title: Evaluation of vegetation drought resistance and resilience across central Asian drylands under water limitation and heat extremes
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Shiran Song, Xi Chen, Akylbek Kurishbayev, Chanjuan Zan, Chuan Wang, Philippe De Maeyer, Shukhrat Shokirov, Imanmadi Duman, Luqmon Samiev, Tie Liu
abstract: Study region Arid Central Asia is one of the largest dryland systems in Eurasia and has experienced amplified warming, increasing drought, and intensifying heat extremes. Yet ecosystem drought stability and its hydroclimatic controls remain insufficiently resolved. Study focus We quantified vegetation drought resistance and resilience across arid Central Asia during 2000–2021 using the transpiration-to-evapotranspiration ratio (TET), a functional indicator of vegetation-regulated water use. Drought events were identified using SPEI3, and heatwaves were characterized by frequency, duration, and cumulative heat. Event-based resistance and post-drought resilience were derived from TET responses to isolated drought events, and machine-learning models coupled with SHAP were used to assess the relative associations of hydroclimatic, edaphic, vegetative, and heatwave-related factors with spatial variation in drought stability. New hydrological insights for the region Drought resistance and resilience showed a significant but relatively weak negative association (r = -0.21, p < 0.001). Forests demonstrated the highest resistance (mean Rt = 0.379), whereas sparse vegetation exhibited the highest resilience (mean Rs = 0.059). Ecohydrological attributions revealed that surface soil moisture was the top-ranking predictor associated with resistance. Conversely, resilience was most closely associated with heatwave duration, precipitation, and soil organic carbon. Heatwave associations differed by dimension: heatwave frequency was positively associated with resistance, whereas longer, more intense heatwaves were negatively associated; resilience showed opposite patterns.

title: A novel framework for estimating probable maximum precipitation events by integrating extreme value theory and storm transposition
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Zixin Yang, Jia Wang, Jiahong Liu, Hao Wang, Chao Mei, Fengping Li, Xinyi Chen
abstract: Study region Beijing Municipal Administrative Center (Beijing MC), China. Study focus To improve the applicability of Probable Maximum Precipitation (PMP) in urban flood protection, this study proposes the concept of Potential Probable Maximum Precipitation Events (PMPE) and develops a dual-pathway estimation framework. Based on rainfall-pattern classification, Extreme Value Theory (EVT) is used to derive statistical extreme-rainfall scenarios, while the WRF model transposes historical extreme storms from neighboring regions to generate physically consistent scenarios. By integrating statistical extremity and atmospheric-process consistency, the most adverse scenario in terms of peak intensity and total rainfall is selected for each rainfall pattern as the final PMPE. New hydrological insights for the region Extreme rainfall in the Beijing MC exhibits strong rainfall-pattern dependence, with historical storms classified into six patterns. The most hazardous PMPE features a short-duration, high-intensity structure, with a total rainfall of 326.2 mm, a maximum 1-hour intensity of 84.8 mm, and a duration of 7 h. EVT and storm transposition exhibit complementary strengths, with the former better capturing statistical extremes and the latter producing more severe scenarios when atmospheric dynamics and topographic effects dominate. These findings indicate that urban precipitation extremes arise from both statistical and physical mechanisms. PMPE therefore extends traditional design rainfall estimates to physically plausible extreme-rainfall processes, providing a more reliable basis for urban flood-risk assessment and infrastructure resilience planning.

title: Explainable deep learning for predicting lake expansion in the Siling Co Endorheic basin: Unraveling driver shifts and hydro-climatic tipping points
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Xiangnan Jing, Rao Zhu, Yunfa Miao
abstract: Study region The Siling Co Endorheic Basin (SCEB) on the central Tibetan Plateau is a critical terminal closed-flow catchment within the Asian Water Tower. Highly sensitive to hydro-climatic water balances, the basin has undergone rapid, cryosphere-fed lake expansion. This expansion coincides with significant regional warming and wetting. Study focus To clarify alpine lake evolution mechanisms and overcome the black-box limitations and phase lags of traditional models, this study forecasts the monthly total lake area sequence of the SCEB (2000–2021). We developed the CAF(PINN) framework, a physics-informed approach that embeds the water balance principle over a hybrid architecture consisting of a 1D-CNN, an attention mechanism, and a frequency-domain multi-layer perceptron. Additionally, we quantified interrelationships within lacustrine hydrological processes and physical tipping points using PLS-SEM and Transformed Generalized Additive Models (TGAM). New hydrological insights The CAF(PINN) framework achieved a high Nash–Sutcliffe Efficiency of 0.91, outperforming benchmark models while preserving physically consistent behavior. The model identified a distinct hydrological transition in 2013, suggesting a regime shift toward a meltwater-dominated system. Prior to 2013, lake variations were largely associated with precipitation fluctuations while the cryosphere buffered thermal inputs. Post-2013, however, rising temperatures were closely linked to increased glacier melt and permafrost thaw as primary contributors to lake recharge. This transition suggests an intensifying, non-linear coupling between cryospheric change and regional hydrology, highlighting the expanding influence of thermal factors on water cycles within the Asian Water Tower.

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and key drivers of potential evapotranspiration across the Yangtze River Basin from 1975 to 2018
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Ting Chen, Feiyu Wang, Huiyuan Liu, Lei Zou, Zhiwei Wang, Ying Fan
abstract: Study region The Yangtze River Basin (YZRB). Study focus As a key indicator of atmospheric evapotranspiration capacity, potential evapotranspiration (ET 0) plays a fundamental role in water-energy exchange processes. This study investigated the spatiotemporal variability and underlying mechanisms of ET 0 in the YZRB. Based on a long-term ET 0 dataset, the sensitivity analysis was conducted to assess the response of ET 0 to meteorological factors influencing its temporal variability, and the Multiscale Geographically Weighted Regression (MGWR) model was implemented to identify the drivers shaping the spatial variability of ET 0. New hydrological insights The mean annual ET 0 in the YZRB from 1975 to 2018 was approximately 930 mm, exhibiting a significant increasing trend of 0.63 mm/yr, with a clear upward shift in mean values after 2003. Temperature (T) dominated the spatial heterogeneity of ET 0 in most seasons except spring, with MGWR spatial regression coefficients (SRC) of 0.466 at the annual scale and exceeding 0.60 at seasonal scales. Besides, solar radiation (RS) had the greatest effect on the temporal variation of ET 0, especially in summer when the temporal sensitivity coefficients (TSC) of ET 0 to RS generally exceeded 1.00. These results highlight the distinct roles of temperature and radiation in shaping the spatiotemporal variability of ET 0 and provide valuable insights for large-scale water resources management under climate change.

title: Reconstructing Holocene high-magnitude outburst floods in the Lancang River (Upper Mekong) Grand Cayon, Southeastern Tibetan Plateau: Implication for hazard assessment
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Yongqiang Guo, Yonggang Ge, Peini Mao, Tao Liu
abstract: Study area Lancang River (Upper Mekong) Grand Canyon, situated on the southeastern Tibetan Plateau, represents a high mountain canyon of Three Parallel Rivers Region. Research focus This study integrates sedimentary, geomorphic, chronological, and hydraulic evidence from outburst flood events in the Lancang River Grand Canyon. Our investigation identified three primary palaeoflood records: fine-grained slackwater deposits, gravel bar deposits, and boulder deposits. These flood deposits with similar geochemical composition implies a same flood source. Outburst floods induced by the upstream two landslide dams were dated to 11.9–6.4 ka. New hydrological insights for the region Holocene outburst flood magnitudes were estimated to 39,500–45,900 m³ /s, exceeding the largest observed flood by 7.5–10 times. Such discharges were generated by partial landslide dam failures that eroded more than 50% of the dam height. Hydrodynamic variations and channel morphology result in lateral accretion and backwater-eddy effects during floods. Bedrock channel erosion occurred preferentially at local topographic features within narrow meander bends. High-magnitude outburst floods generate high shear stress (0.4–1.1 kPa) and unit stream power (4.5–10.5 kW/m²) and play a critical role in the geomorphic evolution of the upper Lancang River. Depth-velocity (DV) metrics from palaeoflood‑based worst‑case scenarios indicate highest hazards (DV> 240 m2/s) for bridges versus backwater flooding (DV< 65 m2/s) for roads/villages. This study provides valuable insights into the assessment of similar cascading flood hazards in the southeastern Tibetan Plateau.

title: Stable snowmelt supply dominates enhanced runoff stability in the Tianshan Mountains of Central Asia
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Xueyan Qin, Xiuliang Yuan, Rafiq Hamdi, Jie Bai, Philippe De Maeyer, Hossein Tabari
abstract: Study region This study focuses on 89 basins in the Tianshan Mountains (TMs). Study focus The strength of seasonal cycle (R) from recently developed Directional Statistics method was employed to quantify the changes in runoff stability (Rrunoff) in the TMs during 1980–2019. ERA5-Land daily and monthly runoff data were validated against station observations and the Tianshan Watershed Streamflow dataset (TSWS) at basins-scale, respectively. Random Forest model (RF) coupled with SHapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) was applied to identify the dominant drivers of Rrunoff changes. New hydrological insights for the region Our results revealed a widespread increase in runoff stability, indicated by a decreasing trend of Rrunoff, across 82% of the basins, with approximately 24% showing significant (p < 0.05) trends. Enhanced runoff stability was characterized by a more uniform intra‑annual runoff distribution and reduced intensity and frequency of runoff extremes. A more even seasonal distribution of snowmelt dominated enhanced runoff stability, as evidenced by decreasing Rsm across 68% of the basins. Rain-to-runoff conversion efficiency declined in 97% of basins, 39% of which exhibited significant declines. This decline was attributed to enhanced actual evapotranspiration associated with vegetation greening. These changes reduced runoff extremes, highlighting the buffering capacity of vegetation in hydrological regulation in arid regions and offering important implications for improving water resources management in the arid TMs.

title: Aridity intensification and regime transition in the Ganga Basin: LULC-spectral attribution, ET/PET divergence, and bias-corrected CMIP6 ensemble projection (2000–2100)
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Kunal Dhadse, Ajit Pratap Singh
abstract: Study region The Ganga Basin is an area of about 860,000 km2 in India that sustains 500 million + inhabitants. The basin spans from the humid Himalayan headwaters to the semi-arid Indo-Gangetic plains. Prior work identified a paradox over 2000–2021: concurrent surface water expansion, declining water indices, and rising aridity index (AI) that lacked a mechanistic explanation. Study focus This study attributes observed hydroclimatic trends and forecasts future aridity trajectories by integrating MODIS-LULC, MODIS-ET, ERA5-Land-PET, and 32-model CMIP6-ensemble under SSP2–4.5 and SSP5–8.5. Analytical tests include: Mann-Kendall, partial correlation, first-order Taylor-decomposition, changepoint-convergence, and delta bias correction. New hydrological understandings of the region Forest expansion (+428 km2/year, Z = 5.25, p < 0.001) and Urban Expansion (+27 km2/year, Z = 6.49, p < 0.001) are the strongest independent partial correlates of decreasing NDWI and MNDWI respectively. Real ET increased, PET decreased, and ET/PET increased across all LULC classes, contributed by expanding irrigation. AI decomposition indicates precipitation intensification as the dominant driver (73.1%) of AI trend. Changepoint tests indicates towards the statistically significant aridity regime shift in 2010–2011 (Pettitt p = 0.014). The CMIP6 ensemble shows a universal wet bias of + 0.202 and no interannual skill retention after bias-correction (r = -0.079, p = 0.78). Ensemble mean projection under SSP2–4.5 and SSP5–8.5) shows an increasing climatological trajectory episodically approaching the sub-humid threshold under both scenarios.

title: Parsimonious climatic and physiographic controls explain the spatial variability of the Budyko parameter
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Yiping Jiang, Kun Yang, Xin Xia, Yuan Yang, Hui Lu
abstract: Study region 532 minimally disturbed catchments in the contiguous United States (CONUS). Study focus The Budyko framework provides a representation of long-term water-energy partitioning. However, its practical application depends on the reliable estimation of the parameter ω, whose dominant controls remain inconsistently identified across regions. Here, we investigate whether a minimal set of climatic and physiographic variables can explain the spatial variability of ω across hydroclimatically diverse catchments. We apply a machine-learning-based variable selection framework to identify indispensable controls and evaluate the influence of hydroclimatic heterogeneity on predictor selection. New hydrological insights Results demonstrate that only four variables—the fraction of precipitation falling as snow, aridity index, precipitation seasonality index, and compound topographic index—are sufficient to capture the majority of the spatial variability of ω across CONUS, while vegetation indices play a relatively minor role. We further show that hydroclimatic heterogeneity can obscure the identification of dominant controls on ω when predictor selection relies solely on correlation-based approaches. Using the four selected controls, we developed both a random forest (RF) model and a multivariate linear regression (MLR) model. Both achieved good performance on independent test basins (RF: R² = 0.80, RMSE = 0.227; MLR: R² = 0.616, RMSE = 0.315), and both substantially outperformed two existing ω parameterizations (Li model: R² = −0.784, RMSE = 0.679; Bai model: R² = −0.099, RMSE = 0.533). When incorporated into the Fu–Budyko equation, the estimated ω reproduces annual runoff variability with high accuracy (R² = 0.94, RMSE = 98.52 mm). These findings demonstrate that much of the large-scale variability of ω can be explained by a small set of hydroclimatic and physiographic controls, providing a physically interpretable and parsimonious basis for Budyko applications in ungauged and data-scarce regions.

title: Estimating environmental water table depth of vegetation in the arid and semi-arid regions of the Balkhash Lake Basin integrating the CatBoost regression and shapley additive explanations
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Feng Huang, Yiping Li, Carlos G. Ochoa, Saparov Galymzhan
abstract: Study Region The Balkhash Lake Basin in Central Asia. Study Focus Estimating the environmental water table depth in arid and semi-arid endorheic basins is fundamental for sustainable groundwater resource management and protecting groundwater-dependent terrestrial ecosystems. However, the assessment is challenging due to the mixed effect of multiple environmental variables on the relationship between vegetation and water table depth. This study aimed to address this gap by utilizing interpretable machine learning, specifically integrating CatBoost regression and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP). The CatBoost algorithm was used to construct the enhanced vegetation index (EVI) and actual evapotranspiration (ET) models, driven by three critical hydrological variables: precipitation (PRE), water table depth (WTD), and potential evapotranspiration (PET), due to an emphasis on hydrological controls on EVI and ET. The SHAP interpretation was used to extract the impact of WTD on EVI and ET from the mixed effects of PRE, WTD, and PET, indicating the environmental water table depth. New hydrological insights for the region Integrating CatBoost regression and SHAP interpretation proved practical for estimating the environmental water table depth in arid and semi-arid endorheic basins. For preserving the groundwater-dependent vegetation, the turning point on the SHAP dependence plot of WTD indicated an environmental water table depth of 8 m, above which WTD contributed to EVI and ET positively and under which EVI and ET were insensitive to WTD variations.

title: Nonlinear responses and differentiated pathways of driving mechanisms underlying the spatiotemporal evolution of water retention in the Qinba Mountains
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Jinxia Zhang, Jiaqi Zhang, Zhao Liu, Duofen Li, Xudong Sun
abstract: Study Region The Qinba Mountains represent a critical water retention area characterized by complex terrain and hydrological heterogeneity. Study Focus This study distinguished high, moderate, and low water retention states and integrated the InVEST model, random forest regression, and piecewise structural equation modeling to systematically analyze the spatiotemporal evolution, key drivers, and causal pathways of water retention. To address the limited monthly representation of baseflow in the InVEST-SWY module, an observation-constrained seasonal allocation approach was further used to disaggregate simulated annual baseflow into monthly values, improving the representation of intra-annual water retention dynamics. New Hydrological Insights for the Region Water retention showed a south-high and north-low spatial pattern, with moderate-to-high water retention levels covering 59.01% of the region. From 2000–2023, water retention remained generally stable, showing a nonsignificant increase of 0.58 mm yr−1. Precipitation was the strongest positive driver, whereas potential evapotranspiration imposed the strongest negative constraint. The dominant regulatory pathways exhibited clear state dependence, shifting from precipitation dominance with vegetation-wind speed synergy in high water retention states to precipitation dominance with strong evapotranspiration limitation in low states, with moderate states representing a transitional regime in which precipitation control coexisted with coordinated topography-vegetation regulation. These findings clarify the dynamic regulation of water retention in the Qinba Mountains and provide scientific support for regional water resource management.

title: Attribution and spatial heterogeneity of groundwater level drivers: Gnangara region in Western Australia
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Feihe Kong, Guobin Fu, Jinghao Wang, Xiaokang Du, Shaohua Zhang, Chao Zhu
abstract: Study Region: The Gnangara region in Western Australia, characterized by a Mediterranean climate with rainfall-dominated recharge, supplies approximately 60% of Perth’s drinking water. Study Focus: This study established spatiotemporal models between GLD and 87 climate and non-climate variables based on a 48-year (1977–2024) dataset from 399 monitoring bores to identify the major drivers of groundwater level differences (GLD) using a progressive statistical framework. New Hydrological Insights for the Region: Results showed: 1) GLD exhibited a significant linear decline (cumulative 0.14 m; multi-year average 0.58 m), driven by long-term drought and sustained abstraction, with a spatial gradient increasing from northwest to southeast, shaped by hydrogeological and climatic gradients. 2) Seasonal climate variables outperformed annual-scale indicators in characterizing groundwater dynamics. Rainfall was the dominant factor influencing GLD, with May-September rainfall positively contributing the most (38.73%), and total rainfall above the 95th percentile threshold contributing 29.87%. June–August potential evaporation (Span68) and mean dry spell length (MeDS) were negatively correlated with GLD, contributing 13.74% and 8.70%, respectively. 3) Among non-climate variables, groundwater abstraction contributed negatively (6.20%), while NDVI had the smallest positive impact (2.76%). Both are scale-dependent, with regional impacts weakened by hydrogeological and climatic heterogeneity. These findings advance groundwater management by supporting targeted strategies: prioritizing seasonal and 95th-percentile rainfall monitoring over annual indicators and implementing permeability-adapted groundwater abstraction management for shallow aquifer dynamics.

title: Flow regime alteration under progressive multi-reservoir development in the Upper Yangtze River basin
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Zaichao Xie, Minglei Ren, Wei Xu, Te Zhang, Bing Zhu, Dong Li, Shuncai Zhang, Yuanyou Ran
abstract: Study Region : The Upper Yangtze River basin, comprising the Jinsha, Min, Jialing, and Wu tributaries and the mainstream, contains 38 large reservoirs with a live storage capacity (LSC) of 80.5 billion m 3 . Study Focus : This study couples hydrological simulation with the Soil and Water Assessment Tool (SWAT) and reservoir-operation optimization to quantify flow regime alteration across three development stages: a natural baseline, a 21-reservoir configuration, and a 38-reservoir configuration. SWAT simulated daily natural flows for 1965–2024, and the Progressive Optimality Algorithm-Dynamic Programming Successive Approximation (POA-DPSA) optimized reservoir operations under a common objective and constraint framework. This counterfactual design isolates reservoir-operation effects from climatic variability and enables comparison among sub-basins with contrasting reservoir layouts and coordination structures. New Hydrological Insights for the Region : Reservoir operations reduced wet-to-dry flow ratios by up to 64.6% through seasonal redistribution. Under the fixed-parameter baseline, DOR (storage-to-annual-runoff ratio) above about 10% was associated with substantial flood attenuation, whereas low-flow augmentation emerged above about 5%. Across the three development stages examined in each basin, DOR and the coefficient of variation (CV) of daily flow were well described by linear fits (R ≥ 0.98), but fitted slopes differed among basins, indicating spatially variable sensitivity to DOR increases across development stages. A coordinated-versus-non-coordinated comparison showed basin-dependent coordination gains, strongest in the Jinsha cascade and weaker where mainstream multi-year reservoirs already provided substantial regulation.

title: Integrating Kalman smoother and hydrodynamic model for accurate estimation of true inflow for river-type reservoirs
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Yang Liu, Pan Liu, Hao Wang, Weibo Liu, Yuan Liu, Wei Zhang, Qian Cheng, Hui Zhao, Chutian Zhou, Huan Xu, Vijay P. Singh
abstract: Study region The Three Gorges Reservoir, China. Study focus Reservoir theoretical “true” inflow estimation is crucial for forecasting and operational decisions. However, in river-type reservoirs where the dam is far from the upstream boundary, flow propagation time lag and information loss reduce inflow estimation accuracy. The study proposed a novel method integrating a Kalman smoother with a 1D hydrodynamic model to estimate theoretical “true” inflow under time-lag conditions. The state transition equations for inflow and water level were developed using a Gaussian random walk and a one-dimensional hydrodynamic model. The hydrodynamic model was executed under varying inflow ensemble members to simulate water levels and flow signal propagation time. The Kalman smoother was employed to update generated inflow ensemble. The proposed method was validated by comparing with water balance (WB), analytical method (AM), and ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF). New hydrological insights for the region (1) The proposed method improved peak flow estimation accuracy by 2∼3%, reduced RMSE by 40∼70% under synthetic experiments, and increased the lateral inflow NSE from 0.717 to 0.909; (2) the effect of time lags was reduced through dynamic estimation of the flow propagation time and backward propagation of information in both synthetic and real cases, while WB and EnKF underperformed. The proposed method provides a reliable solution for theoretical “true” inflow estimation, supporting more effective reservoir management.

title: A "Background-Dynamics-Loss-Resilience" framework to assess flood risk in the Shandong reach of the Lower Yellow River
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Zhonggang Miao, Siqi Li, Hengheng Song, Binru Zhao, Xudong Zhou, Teng Zhong, Pingping Luo, Zhaoyuan Yu, Longhui Li, Wenchao Ma
abstract: Study region The downstream sub-basin of the Lower Yellow River in Shandong Province. Study focus Flood risk in suspended-river systems remains poorly understood due to their anomalous geomorphology and hydrodynamic behavior. This study integrates a two-dimensional hydrodynamic model with a multi-source Background-Dynamics-Loss-Resilience (BDLR) framework to assess flood risk in suspended river systems. Flood inundation processes for return periods of 5–100 years were simulated to quantify the spatiotemporal responses of inundation depth and flow velocity. A hybrid weighting approach, combining Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and Entropy Weight Method (EWM), was applied to determine the relative importance of various factors in flood risk. Spatial risk distribution maps were generated, and dynamic threshold analysis identified risk-sensitive areas for targeted flood prevention. New hydrological insights for the region Floodwaters in suspended river systems overtop topographic ridges in stages, resulting in diminishing marginal increases in inundated area with increasing return period. Flood risk is controlled by geomorphic constraints and energy redistribution. Key risk factors include slope (14.868%-15.899%), inundation depth (16.371%-17.004%), flow velocity (14.380%-15.695%), population and GDP density (27.382%-28.570%). About 8.09% of the region exhibits higher- and high-risk values (> 0.279) under low return period (5-year) flood scenarios, indicating high sensitivity to such floods, particularly in the Jindi River basin, the Yellow River estuary. These findings offer new insights for flood management in the Shandong reach.

title: Development of a novel spatiotemporal propagation function for flood risk prediction in the Daqing River basin, China
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Shengce Jia, Wei Fang, Qiang Huang, Quan Quan, Xiangxiang Jiang, Jie Zhang, Liangbo Zhang, Xin Xu, Jingru Zhang
abstract: Study region The Daqing River basin in China has been frequently affected by floods. Flood risk exhibits both temporal and spatial interdependence, driven by hydrological memory effects and cascading flood processes within spatially connected river systems. Study focus The study elucidated spatiotemporal propagation patterns of flood risk and developed a novel spatiotemporal propagation function for risk prediction. Initially, flood risk in twenty-two subbasins of the Daqing River was evaluated by integrating hazard, exposure, vulnerability and mitigation capacity. Markov-based state transition diagrams were subsequently employed to calculate flood risk propagation probabilities, distinguishing temporal and spatial risk propagation patterns. Moreover, a spatiotemporal risk propagation function incorporating risk propagation effect and flood control infrastructure interference was proposed to predict flood risk. New hydrological insights Results indicate pronounced spatial heterogeneity in flood risk across the Daqing River basin during 2000–2020, with high-risk areas concentrated in northern region and eastern edge. Temporally, interannual flood risk variation in each subbasin was driven by mid-high and high, and low and medium grade transitions. Spatial propagation between adjacent subbasins was dominated by risk attenuation across 44.8% of adjacent subbasins. The spatiotemporal propagation function achieved an average prediction accuracy of 90.5% and disentangled temporal and spatial propagation contributions to flood risk. Additionally, five reservoirs and flood detention areas in the central-eastern basin reduced risk propagation by 26.4% and 30.3% via their buffering capacities.

title: Revealing the value of water resources in the Yellow River Basin at the city scale: An integrated framework bridging historical insights, future trends and practical applications
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Zheng Wu, Jinyi Zhang, Jiawen Li, Guiliang Tian
abstract: Study region The Yellow River Basin(YRB), a region in China characterized by significant water scarcity and intense human activity. Study focus Water resource value(WRV) serves as a critical signal and instrument for supporting governance decision-making. This study developed an integrated framework bridging historical insights, future trends, and practical applications, employed the fuzzy comprehensive evaluation method to quantify WRV at the city scale in the YRB and reveal its spatiotemporal characteristics, applied Geographically and Temporally Weighted Regression (GTWR) to examine the influencing factors of WRV, and further used time-series forecasting and machine learning models to predict both WRV and its determinants, ultimately constructed a zonal governance framework based on the Water Supply Index (WSI), Water Demand Index (WDI), and WRV to provide prospective governance recommendations for cities in different zones. New hydrological insights for the region The results indicated pronounced spatial heterogeneity in WRV across the YRB along both east-west and north-south directions. In the early study period, cities in the western YRB exhibited higher WRV than those in the east, whereas this pattern reversed in the later period. Meanwhile, cities in the northern YRB consistently showed higher WRV than those in the south. GTWR results revealed that supply-side factors exerted a stronger overall influence on WRV than demand-side factors, with annual precipitation, technological innovation capacity, and mean elevation ranking as the top three supply-side determinants, and industrial upgrading level, industrialization level, and social consumption level ranking as the top three demand-side determinants. Predictions indicated that WRV in approximately 60% of cities is likely to decline slightly in the future, suggesting that supply-demand tensions in some regions may be alleviated under strengthened water-saving constraints and improved utilization efficiency. Finally, a four-quadrant zonal governance framework was constructed based on the predicted WSI, WDI, and WRV. By treating WRV as both a governance signal and a governance instrument, zone-specific governance recommendations were proposed to support differentiated water resource management and high-quality development in the YRB.

title: Water level dynamics monitoring for the lakes on the Yunnan plateau by using surface water and ocean topography (SWOT) satellite data
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Xin Luo, Ziyue Dou, Kecheng Yang, Nan Xu
abstract: Study region This study focuses on the Yunnan Plateau in southwestern China, examining nine major plateau lakes: Dianchi, Erhai, Fuxian Hu, Chenghai, Lugu Hu, Qilu Hu, Xingyun Hu, Yangzonghai, and Yilong Hu, all located in high-altitude settings with complex surrounding terrain. Study focus Using newly released Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) satellite data to monitor lake water-level dynamics, we propose an automated method to retrieve high-precision time-series water levels from SWOT observations. The method aims to improve spatiotemporal monitoring capability and provide a complementary alternative to the official SWOT LakeSP product. New hydrological insights for the region The results show that SWOT, combined with the proposed method, can monitor the nine lakes at a monthly scale with high accuracy (achieving an RMSE of less than 0.09 m). The retrieved water levels reveal clear seasonal variations, with minimum levels generally occurring in April–May and maxima from August to November, consistent with regional precipitation patterns. Intra-annual water-level fluctuations range from 0.23 to 1.20 m. Most lakes exhibit periodic annual variations, whereas Fuxian Hu and Yangzonghai show sustained water-level declines over the available observation period.

title: Quantifying drought impacts on irrigation water requirements across major crops and growth stages in the Yellow River Basin
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Qifan Pan, Zhongwei Huang, Jinkai Luan, Guoyong Leng
abstract: Study region The Yellow River Basin, China. Study focus Irrigation plays a critical role in sustaining agricultural development, particularly in water-scarce regions such as the Yellow River Basin (YRB). Yet, the response of irrigation water requirement (IWR) to drought events across different crop types and growth stages remained inadequately characterized. Here, we developed a daily-scale, multi-crop simulation framework that integrated the FAO Penman-Monteith method and the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) to assess the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of IWR responses to drought events across four major crops (wheat, maize, rice, and soybeans) in the YRB during 1980–2018, which enabled systematic comparison of drought impacts across crop types and growth stages. New hydrological insights Drought significantly increased IWR for all crops, with basin-average increases of 27.70–31.36% during drought periods compared to non-drought periods. IWR increased consistently with drought severity, corroborated by significant linear correlations between SPEI and IWR anomaly, particularly in the Wei River Basin characterized by intensive irrigation and severe drought conditions. Specifically, rice exhibited the strongest sensitivity to drought across all growth stages, whereas the mid-season stage was identified as the most critical period for drought-induced IWR amplification for most crops. These findings moved beyond aggregate drought-impact assessments to provide an explicit understanding of irrigation sensitivity to drought, offering a scientific basis for targeted water allocation and drought adaptation strategies in water-stressed regions.

title: Estimating groundwater evapotranspiration under pumping conditions using diurnal groundwater level fluctuations
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Jinting Huang, Tian Huang, Wenke Wang
abstract: Study region Hailiutu River catchment, semi-arid region of northwestern China. Study focus It remains challenge to estimate ETg during pumping. The White method estimates ETg from diurnal groundwater-level fluctuations and is widely applied in arid and semi-arid regions because of its simplicity and low cost. However, groundwater extraction substantially reduces the reliability of the White method and its variants. This study used numerical simulations to analyze groundwater diurnal fluctuation time-series components under different extraction conditions and evaluated an ETg estimation framework integrating Dynamic Harmonic Regression (DHR) with the Boussinesq equation. The effects of different extraction scenarios on groundwater diurnal fluctuation components and ETg estimation were systematically analyzed. New hydrological insights for the region Results indicate that groundwater evapotranspiration (ETg) in the study area is the primary discharge item of groundwater. Under non-pumping condition, estimation results indicate that average ETg is 6.92 mm/d. While, under continuous extraction conditions, the estimated mean value of ETg is 6.68 mm/d. Beyond documenting ETg estimation results, this study provides an operational perspective by integration DHR and analytical solution of Boussinesq equation to estimate ETg used under groundwater extraction condition. By relying on numerical simulation results from the research site, the study demonstrates how pumping patterns affect the estimation accuracy of ETg. The integrated framework offers an effective approach for ETg estimation to isolate pumping disturbance in semi-arid vegetation regions.

title: Data-driven vulnerability assessment of the Nansi Lake Basin water resource system
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Zhenxiang Xu, Linjing Wu, Xiao Li, Yanfang Diao, Junnuo Wang, Qingtai Qiu, Jiyang Tian, Rumeng Liang
abstract: Study region Nansi Lake Basin, a water-scarce region in northern China. Study focus This study conducted a data-driven vulnerability assessment of the Nansi Lake Basin water resource system. The Driver–Pressure–State–Impact–Response conceptual model was applied to define a three-tier vulnerability evaluation system comprising a target layer, 5 first-level indicators, and 26 second‐level indicators. Particle swarm optimization (PSO) was employed to determine the optimal hyperparameters of a long short-term memory (LSTM) network trained on data comprising randomly generated evaluation indicator values and their corresponding vulnerability grading standards. This hybrid PSO–LSTM model was used to assess the spatiotemporal vulnerability of the Nansi Lake Basin water resource system from 2010 to 2021, and its rationality was verified by comparison with the variable fuzzy assessment method. New hydrological insights for the region The hybrid PSO–LSTM model exhibited high accuracy (R 2 > 0.999 for both training and validation samples) and stability, indicating its suitability for vulnerability assessments. Temporally, the vulnerabilities in the Nansi Lake Basin and its six subregions fluctuated downward over the study period, evolving from highly vulnerable in 2010 to slightly vulnerable by 2021. Spatially, vulnerability decreased faster in the western than eastern subregions. Finally, the obstacle degree model identified the causes of vulnerability to provide a scientific foundation for the utilization and management of water resources in the Nansi Lake Basin.

title: Reconstructing inland lake bathymetry in optically complex waters by fusing ICESat-2 altimetry and Sentinel-2 Imagery: A case study of Lake Balkhash
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Ruibiao Yang, Jinglu Wu
abstract: Study region Lake Balkhash, a large endorheic lake in southeastern Kazakhstan, Central Asia, with strong spatial variation in water clarity. Study focus Accurate lake water storage estimation in arid regions requires reliable bathymetry, but large optically complex lakes remain difficult to map because of limited in situ data and rapid signal attenuation. This study develops a bathymetric retrieval framework for Lake Balkhash by integrating ICESat-2 photon-counting LiDAR and multi-temporal Sentinel-2 imagery. An adaptive DBSCAN-based algorithm was used to extract lakebed photons from noisy photon clouds, and the resulting depth samples were combined with Sentinel-2 spectral features in a Random Forest model to produce a continuous high-resolution bathymetric map. New hydrological insight for the region The proposed fusion framework performed well in reconstructing lakebed topography under varying water-clarity conditions, achieving an RMSE of 1.046 m against independent in situ validation data. The reconstructed bathymetry reveals clear morphological differences between the two sub-basins, suggesting that the shallow western sub-basin is more sensitive to hydrological fluctuations than the deeper saline eastern sub-basin. By establishing level–area–volume relationships, we reconstructed a long-term record of lake water storage changes. This record indicates a renewed decline in water storage during 2019–2024. These findings demonstrate the limitations of traditional area-based monitoring and provide a volumetric baseline for water resource assessment in Central Asia.

title: Event-based evaluation of gridded precipitation datasets in the Zayu River Basin, Southeastern Tibetan Plateau
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Kaiwen Li, Dawei Xiao, Junzhi Liu, Wanhong Yang, Bin Zhang, Zhengxu Guo, Zheng Duan, Yongqin Liu
abstract: Study region The Zayu River Basin in the southeastern Tibetan Plateau. Study focus Utilizing a dense network of 18 newly deployed rain gauges, this study characterizes spatiotemporal rainfall variability and evaluates six gridded precipitation products. We integrated multi-scale assessments (daily to hourly) with an event-based error decomposition framework to diagnose systematic biases in satellite and reanalysis datasets. New hydrological insights for the region: Observations reveal early-morning rainfall peaks and substantial spatial heterogeneity. At the daily scale, gauge-based CHM (China Hydro-Meteorology Precipitation) outperforms others. For all the hourly products, evaluations expose a distinct spatial disparity: western tributaries exhibit higher detection skill, while eastern tributaries suffer severe overestimation. Specifically, GMCP (Global Multisource Merging-and-Calibration Precipitation) proves most robust. Error decomposition reveals that ERA5-Land (the land component of the fifth-generation ECMWF atmospheric reanalysis) biases stem from "drizzle effects" (false-end errors), whereas IMERG (Integrated Multi-satellite Retrievals for Global Precipitation Measurement) biases arise from stochastic detection failures (miss-events). These diagnostics offer critical guidance for correcting precipitation data in data-scarce alpine regions.

title: Climate and land-use drivers of future flood exposure and damage in the Cagayan River Basin, Philippines
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Yuta Kurihara, Mamoru Miyamoto, Ryoya Kyuzaki
abstract: Study region. The Cagayan Valley Region (Region II) in northern Luzon, Philippines, includes the Cagayan River Basin, the country’s longest river system and largest catchment. The basin is a major rice- and corn-producing area, but recurrent tropical-cyclone and monsoon floods cause damage almost every year. Study focus. This study assesses future flood hazard, exposure, and private-sector damage by integrating climate, land-use, and population scenarios within a common time frame. Climate forcing came from three CMIP6 GCMs – ACCESS-CM2, CanESM5, and EC-Earth3-Veg-LR – under four SSPs, and bias-corrected rainfall drove the RRI model. Future land use was projected by combining Land Change Modeler susceptibility scores with population- and crop-area demand constraints, while population distribution was estimated from government projections and spatial covariates. By overlaying projected land use, population, and inundation, the study quantifies crop-specific exposure, separates climate- and land-use-driven contributions, and evaluates land-use regulation. New hydrological insights. This integrated assessment shows that simulated peak discharge increases across all future SSP scenarios because rainfall events exhibit higher short-duration intensity and sharper temporal peaks. The 100-year inundated area increases by more than 31% under higher-forcing scenarios. Under the medium population scenario, exposed population increases by about 100%, from approximately 1 million at present to 2 million by 2070. Climate change mainly increases frequent-flood exposure, whereas land-use expansion amplifies rare-flood exposure and damage. Risk-informed land-use regulation reduces future housing losses by up to 154 million PHPyr−1.

title: Spatiotemporal variations and driver-specific response characteristics of evapotranspiration across different vegetation types in the Qilian Mountains
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Xinrui Wang, Guofeng Zhu, Lincheng Li, Lifang Chou, Zhi Wang, Zhong Luo, Zengtian Hou, Junhao Zhao, Wenxiong Jia
abstract: Study region The Qilian Mountains, northwestern China Study focus Using the PML-V2.8 evapotranspiration (ET) dataset together with hydroclimatic, vegetation, and topographic variables, this study examined the spatiotemporal variations of ET across forests, shrublands, and grasslands in the Qilian Mountains during 2000–2022. Ensemble machine-learning models combined with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were further used to identify dominant controls, monthly shifts in driving factors, and response patterns among different vegetation types. New hydrological insights for the region From 2000–2022, ET increased significantly in the Qilian Mountains, mainly in spring and summer. Forest ET increased fastest, whereas grassland ET showed the strongest interannual variability. The dominant controls differed among vegetation types: forest and shrubland ET were mainly regulated by hydroclimatic factors, particularly solar radiation, whereas grassland ET was jointly constrained by energy conditions and elevation-related topographic gradients represented by DEM. Monthly SHAP analysis revealed clear seasonal shifts in dominant controls, with LAI dominating forest and shrubland ET during June-August and DEM dominating grassland ET in most months. Response curves indicated no strong nonlinear responses or clear threshold effects, highlighting the combined roles of vegetation type, seasonal driver shifts, and topographic constraints in regulating ET across mountainous ecosystems.

title: Analysis of drought events in the Jiziwan region of the Yellow River basin and their responses to atmospheric circulation factors on the basis of a three-dimensional identification algorithm
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Sinan Wang, Xigang Xing, Yingjie Wu, Jianying Guo, Xuning Guo, Ping Miao
abstract: Study region Jiziwan region of the Yellow River basin, China. Study focus In the Yellow River basin, ecological protection and the development of high-quality infrastructure are of great strategic significance for China. To date, the ecological protection of the Yellow River basin has faced severe challenges, among which frequent droughts have become key limiting factors. However, the spatiotemporal structure and occurrence pattern of drought in the Jiziwan region of the Yellow River basin are difficult to accurately represent, and the mechanisms by which the driving factors affect drought are unknown. Therefore, in this study, the temperature–vegetation drought index (TVDI), 3D drought identification algorithm, structural equation modelling (SEM) system and multivariate cross-wavelet transform were used to reveal the spatiotemporal characteristics of drought events and their response mechanisms to driving factors New hydrological insights for the region From 2001–2020, the annual TVDI increased significantly (0.011/year), with a spatial distribution showing a pattern of higher values in the west and lower values in the east. Seasonal differences were evident, with spring being the most severe drought season and winter showing the fastest increase in TVDI (0.012/year). A total of 15 drought events were identified, with the 2015–2016 event being the most severe (24-month duration, 52.58% of the area affected, and an intensity of 4.635 ×105 km²·month). Soil moisture mitigates drought through direct and indirect pathways, while surface temperature and solar radiation exacerbate drought via energy balance processes. Precipitation is the key negative moderator of drought, with the largest total impact (-0.69), highlighting its critical role in alleviating drought. Atmospheric circulation factors (AO, DMI, PNA) interact with drought (TVDI) through multiple timescale resonance cycles (4–56 months), collectively influencing drought development by altering regional water-heat balance.

title: Using remotely sensed evapotranspiration to identify groundwater discharge areas in northern Australia
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Russell S. Crosbie, Andrew R. Taylor, Jodie L. Pritchard
abstract: Study region The study region is the catchments that overlie, and are adjacent to, the Cambrian Limestone Aquifer in northern Australia. Study focus The Cambrian Limestone Aquifer is the largest water resource in the Northern Territory, and the only reliable water resource in the region. Water resources development has historically only occurred in the Daly and Roper catchments, but there are now increasing development pressures on the water resources in other catchments. The groundwater discharge through springs is culturally, ecologically and economically important and protected through water allocation plans. The springs in the Daly and Roper have been well characterised but the other sparsely populated, undeveloped catchments, have not had the same level of investigation. This study aims to use remotely sensed evapotranspiration to identify groundwater discharge areas across ∼750,000 km2 of northern Australia. New hydrological insights for the region The current conceptualisation of the CLA has discharge occurring in the Roper, Daly and Nicholson catchments. This study has identified small groundwater discharge locations at the basin margins in the Victoria, Limmen Bight, McArthur, Robinson and Calvert catchments. These additional groundwater discharge locations need to be assessed for their source aquifer before development occurs in these regions to ensure the protection of their cultural, ecological and economic values.

title: Analysis of the lag response of rainfall erosivity to typical climate indices using a dynamically weighted ensemble model
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Yurong Mu, Dayun Zhu, Zulun Zhao, Wanqing Liu, Jiaying Tan
abstract: Study region Southern China Study focus This study employed the Distributed Lag Non-linear Model (DLNM) and a dynamically weighted ensemble model to investigate the lag response mechanisms of rainfall erosivity to typical climate indices in Southern China. New hydrological insights for the region The results indicate that: (1) Significant variations exist in the lag responses of rainfall erosivity to typical climate indices across Southern China. Rainfall erosivity responds relatively rapidly to the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) and the Arctic Oscillation (AO), with lag times concentrated between 1 and 4 months. Conversely, lag times for the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD), Western Hemisphere Warm Pool (WHWP), and Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO) are generally longer, exceeding 4 months in most regions. (2) Air pressure (PRES), downward longwave radiation (LRAD), downward shortwave radiation (SRAD) temperature (TMP), and erosive rainfall (ER) are identified as the core factors influencing the lag effects of rainfall erosivity. Their threshold characteristics vary depending on the climatic background; specifically, when PRES exceeds 915 hPa, the lag time of rainfall erosivity to ENSO shortens, while the lag time to AO is extended. (3) Independent contributions from factors such as Digital Elevation Model (DEM), relative humidity (RHU), and the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) are relatively weak. These factors primarily exert local regulatory effects on the lag responses through interactions with meteorological factors.

title: Scale dependent effects and threshold identification of key influencing factors on runoff and sediment in the Wei River Basin
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Mengyao Tuo, Guoce Xu, Mingzhu Xu, Zaixing Zhi, Jing Li, Bin Wang, Fengyou Gu, Yuxi Wei
abstract: Study region Wei River Basin, a typical erosion prone basin on the Chinese Loess Plateau, northwestern China. Study focus Based on eight watersheds within Wei River Basin, the separate and joint contributions of climate, land surface composition (e.g. vegetation coverage, land use and land cover change) and landscape configuration were quantified across different spatial scales. Subsequently, their sensitivity were evaluated and threshold behaviors were identified. New hydrological insights for the region Runoff and sediment reductions since the early 21st century were mainly associated with human activities. Across spatial scales, landscape configuration exhibited stronger independent contributions (approximately 15∼21%) than precipitation (3%∼7%) and land surface composition (3%∼5%). Clear scale dependence was observed, with the highest explanatory power at the 500 m buffer scale, where combined factors explained up to 84.8% of runoff and sediment. Furthermore, sediment load showed stronger sensitivities than runoff to key factors. Among the tested factors, LSI was identified as the most sensitive factor, with a 1% increase being associated with relative increases of 1.60% in runoff and 2.46% in sediment load, respectively. Moreover, runoff and sediment load may undergo sudden changes once key landscape metrics exceed critical values. These findings reveal the importance of spatial structure and scale effects in regulating runoff and sediment processes in erosion dominated watersheds.

title: Improving SWAT model performance and characterization of water cycle components through dual-objective spatially distributed calibration of streamflow and evapotranspiration
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Meiling Zheng, Jiao Chen, Xingwei Chen, Weifang Ruan, Xiaocheng Li, Huaxia Yao, Yunpeng Gao, Bingqing Lin, Kaili Geng, Haijun Deng, Ying Chen, Meibing Liu
abstract: Study region Shaxi River Basin of China. Study focus Accurate simulation of water cycle components is critical for understanding basin hydrological processes and supporting water resources management. This study evaluates the performance of the SWAT model under two calibration strategies: dual-objective lumped calibration of streamflow and evapotranspiration (ET) (M1) and dual-objective spatially distributed calibration (M2). Model calibration and validation were conducted using observed outlet streamflow and spatially distributed ET data, and terrestrial water storage change (TWSC) was estimated based on water balance analysis. New hydrological insights for the region Both calibration strategies reproduce the temporal dynamics of streamflow and ET, while M2 demonstrates consistently superior performance. For streamflow, M2 improves NSE from 0.73 to 0.94 during calibration and from 0.51 to 0.89 during validation, with PBIAS reduced from 15.04–17.45% to 3.79–5.10%. For ET, PBIAS decreases from −3.31% to 0.69% during calibration and from −7.98% to −2.79% during validation. Spatially, M2 enhances sub-basin ET simulation, with NSE generally increasing and systematic biases reduced across most sub-basins. ET-related parameters exhibit physically consistent relationships with soil types and vegetation cover, indicating improved representation of underlying surface heterogeneity. Long-term simulations reveal pronounced spatial gradients, with precipitation and runoff decreasing from northwest to southeast, ET increasing from west to east, and TWSC showing relatively limited spatial variability. Overall, spatially distributed dual-objective calibration improves both the accuracy and spatial consistency of water cycle simulations, providing a robust framework for hydrological modeling in heterogeneous basins.

title: Extreme minimum temperature and precipitation indices drive the shortening of snow cover duration in China
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Hang Wu, Qiuli Yang, Yuhao Feng, Xiaoyong Wu, Haoxuan Liu, Yuping Li, Changchun Xu
abstract: Study region This research focuses on China's stable snow cover regions, encompassing the Mid-Temperate Arid, Semi-Arid, and Semi-Humid Zones, alongside the Plateau Temperate Semi-Arid Zone. Spanning 1980–2019, this domain constitutes a critical component of global hydrological and energy cycles, demonstrating pronounced susceptibility to recent warming trends. Study focus To address the insufficient quantification of snow characteristic (SC) responses to extreme climate, we analyzed snow onset date (SOD), snow end date (SED), and snow cover duration (SCD). Using an integrated framework of trend analysis, Random Forest, and Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), we disentangled the interplay between SC and extreme indices while accounting for mean warming. New hydrological insights for the region The analysis reveals pervasive snow contraction, with SCD shortening by −2.56 days/5a. The annual minimum daily minimum temperature (TNn) and continuous dry days (CDD) emerge as primary drivers. Other factors regulate snow by modulating these extremes: Leaf Area Index for low vegetation (LAI-LV) influences TNn to delay snow phenology, while nitrous oxide (N2O) affects CDD to advance SED and truncate the snow season. These findings decode complex driver-climate interactions, supporting refined snow modeling under climate warming.

title: Tracking lakeshore wetland changes in China using Sentinel satellite data from 2019 to 2023
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Yajie Chen, Zongming Wang, Ling Luo, Yanzhu Fu, Dehua Mao
abstract: Study region The lakes with area larger than 100 km2 in China Study focus A novel method integrating time-series Sentinel imagery (2019–2023) with an inundation frequency-based classification algorithm was developed to obtain the spatial distribution of lakeshore wetlands (LSWs). By applying the developed method, a spatial distribution dataset of China's LSWs with a 10-meter spatial resolution for the period of 2019–2023 was established. The spatiotemporal patterns of China's LSWs were further investigated based on the dataset and the driving mechanism of variations in LSWs under the extreme climatic conditions was discussed. The research findings were expected to support water environment management, biodiversity conservation, and watershed sustainable development. New hydrological insights Mapping results revealed that LSWs exhibit distinct spatial heterogeneity, with denser distributions in humid southeastern China. A net LSWs area loss of 2769.50 km² occurred during the study period, primarily resulting from dramatic lake shrinkage in the Eastern Plains (EP) ecoregion. Basin runoff constituted the primary controlling factor nationwide, while temperature and snowmelt exerted stronger influences in cold zones, and precipitation–evaporation dynamics dominated in arid regions. Alternating droughts and floods can lead to more frequent changes in hydrologic processes and an increase in the magnitude of water level changes in LSWs. The variations of LSWs caused by the hydrological changes would cause notable ecological effects including changes in waterbird habitat and greenhouse gas emissions.

title: Urban–rural flood risk inequality in Pakistan: Coupling social vulnerability and flood susceptibility
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Lihong Yang, Jing Tan, Xin Yao, Zhangjie Li, Zhiqiang Xie, Shiyin Liu, Zhiqun Hou
abstract: Study region Pakistan, South Asia Study focus Against the backdrop of global climate change, rapid urbanization, and persistent urban–rural development disparities, Pakistan has experienced a sustained increase in flood frequency and the magnitude of associated losses. However, the spatial distributions of the country’s Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) and Flood Susceptibility Index (FSI), along with their coupled interactions, remain insufficiently characterized, thereby constraining the design of targeted disaster prevention and mitigation strategies. To this end, we developed an urban–rural flood risk assessment framework (URSV-FS). First, we constructed the urban–rural SVI using principal component analysis (PCA) and estimated the FSI using an Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model. We then integrated SVI and FSI to derive flood risk and examined the spatial coupling between the two indices. Finally, nighttime light (NTL) remote-sensing data capturing the 2022 extreme flood event were used to validate the risk results and assess urban–rural flood resilience. New hydrological insights for the region The results indicate that: (1) Rural SVI was significantly higher than urban SVI. The proportion of rural districts with very high SVI was 25.4%, and the spatial variability was closely related to socioeconomic development level. (2) The XGBoost model performed well, with an AUC of 0.948 and an accuracy of 0.877. Soil type (SHAP = 0.833), NDVI (SHAP = 0.662), and slope (SHAP = 0.634) were the most influential predictors of FSI. The model classified 24.4% of the study area as high FSI, primarily along river corridors on the Indus Plain and in highly urbanized areas. (3) Flood risk was widespread in rural areas: 13.9% of rural districts were classified as very high risk, and 12.09% of the districts simultaneously exhibited high SVI and high FSI; both proportions were significantly higher than in urban areas. (4) During the flood disaster period, the decline in NTL in rural areas was 2.4 times larger than that in urban areas. However, after the disaster, the recovery of NTL in urban was 2.7 times larger than that in rural, suggesting a weaker recovery capacity in rural areas.

title: Divergent responses of hysteresis loops and sediment sources to rainfall regimes in karst small watersheds of Southwest China: A multi-method integrated framework for classifying erosive rainfall patterns
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Xianwen Zhang, Kunqian Yue, Jiacheng Lan, Rui Li, Yongxiang Jiang, Ruitao Mao, Ya Zhang, Hui Dong
abstract: Study region A typical karst small watershed in Southwest China. Study focus Rainfall patterns regulate runoff–sediment dynamics, yet the mechanisms linking specific patterns to hydro-sedimentary regimes and sediment sources remain unclear. This study utilized a multi-method approach—including Pearson correlation, Random Forest(RF), and Partial Least Squares Regression(PLSR)—to identify the dominant rainfall variables driving runoff–sediment yield from 79 erosive rainfall events (2018–2022). Erosive rainfall patterns were classified to evaluate the subsequent responses of hydro-sedimentary processes and sediment source contributions. New hydrological insights for the region The results indicate that rainfall amount (P), rainfall duration (Dr), and rainfall erosivity (R) are the primary drivers influencing runoff–sediment yield. Using K-means clustering, rainfall events were classified into three patterns (A, B, and C). Pattern A (short duration, moderate erosivity) occurred most frequently (79.75%) and accounted for the highest cumulative runoff–sediment yield. Conversely, Pattern B, though less frequent (7.59%), generated the maximum runoff–sediment yield per event. Hysteresis loop analysis revealed significant variations across rainfall regimes: Pattern A exhibited clockwise loops, Pattern B showed complex loops, and Pattern C displayed counterclockwise loops. Notably, 68% of events exhibited clockwise or complex hysteresis loops, indirectly infers that the subsurface riverbed and conduits are the primary sediment sources. This study provides a theoretical framework for targeted soil erosion control and watershed management in karst regions.

title: Compound dry and hot events in subregions of mainland China and the evolving dynamics from synoptic to sub-seasonal perspective
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Yali Zhu, Xianghui Kong, Yang Liu, Huopo Chen, Jianqi Sun, Xiao Tang
abstract: Study region This study focuses on ten climate-geographical subregions of China, using daily 30-day Standardized Precipitation-Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) and daily maximum temperature data (1961–2018). Compound dry and hot events (CDHEs) are more frequent in western northeastern China, South China, eastern northwestern China, and Northeast China. Study focus While previous studies have emphasized seasonal or monthly scales, this research addresses the critical gap in understanding CDHEs at the synoptic-subseasonal scale—directly relevant to hydrological disaster prediction and early warning—by analyzing dry/hot/CDHE metrics and evolving processes of long-lasting events with emphasis on land-atmosphere interactions and atmospheric circulations. New hydrological insights for the region Hot days increased nationwide, but CDHE days show no significant trend in most subregions due to compensating dry day reductions, challenging simplistic assumptions about compound extremes under global warming. Mechanistically, distinct land–atmosphere pathways dominate across hydroclimatic zones: latent heat flux (LH) governs energy partitioning in humid/semi-humid areas while sensible heat flux (SH) prevails in arid/semi-arid areas. For large-scale circulations, southeastward migration of anomalous anticyclones dominates northern subregions pre-CDHE, whereas local anomalous anticyclones are more critical in southern subregions. These findings fill key knowledge gaps in synoptic-subseasonal CDHE dynamics, offer novel evidence for heterogeneous regional hydrological responses to global warming, and provide actionable insights for advancing short-to-medium-range hydrological disaster prediction and region-specific water resource management strategies.

title: Regional hydraulic controls on flood wave propagation post-impoundment: Insights from the Three Gorges Reservoir for regulated river systems
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Yancheng Han, Wenguang Luo, Jun Xia, Jinxiao Zhao, Yanjun Zhang, Liping Zhang, Jie Liu
abstract: Study region The Three Gorges Reservoir (TGR), a large channel-type reservoir on the Yangtze River, extends 595.6 km from Cuntan to the dam and is strongly influenced by longitudinal backwater. Study focus This study investigated how impoundment alters flood-wave propagation and travel time in the TGR, using a calibrated 1D hydrodynamic model combined with a physically based wave celerity framework under multi-scenario conditions. New hydrological insights for the region Impoundment shifted the dominant control of flood propagation from discharge (kinematic-wave behavior pre-impoundment) to reservoir water level (dynamic-wave behavior under backwater). Near-dam wave celerity increased to ∼19 m/s at high levels, reducing mean travel time from ∼39 h (pre-impoundment) to ∼15 h at 175 m. The proposed celerity formulation agreed well with model results (R² = 0.61), and improved significantly (R² = 0.90) when using model-derived pre-impoundment celerity. These findings provide a physical basis for flood travel time estimation in regulated rivers and support forecasting and reservoir operation.

title: Machine-learning-based regionalization and CMIP6 ensemble projections of precipitation extremes across Pakistan
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Muhammad Abbas, Hamd Ullah, Firdos Khan
